open_questions/1.rationale: This is the cleanest available natural experiment on how FGFR2 transmembrane substitutions are read out, and it is unresolved. Substitutions at FGFR2 Tyr-381 have been reported to cause either Crouzon syndrome or bent bone dysplasia depending on which residue is introduced, so position alone does not determine the disease. The plausible discriminator is the biophysical character of the substituting residue — a cysteine enabling intermolecular disulfide bonding and constitutive dimerization versus a polar residue disrupting membrane insertion and trafficking — but no study cited here compares the two classes side by side in one system, and the nucleolar relocalization arm has not been tested in the gain-of-function alleles at all. It matters for the knowledge base as well as for biology: the FGFR-Related Skeletal Dysplasias grouping admits members on constitutive receptor activation, so whether a given transmembrane allele belongs is a mechanistic question that cannot be settled from the domain it sits in.

evidence.snippet: pain episodes can be triggered by fatigue, bad weather, and cold temperatures
evidence.explanation: Records cold as a clinical trigger of episodes.

evidence.snippet: The pain is often induced by fa- tigue and is a prelude of bad weather
evidence.explanation: Establishes fatigue and impending weather change as episode triggers.

evidence.snippet: Gain-of-function mutations in the human SCN11A-encoded voltage-gated Na(+) channel NaV1.9 cause severe pain disorders
evidence.explanation: States the causal relationship between gain-of-function SCN11A variants and pain disorders.

steps/3.description: A germline missense variant in one SCN11A allele alters the NaV1.9 channel protein. The variant class matters: these are point substitutions that change gating, not alleles that remove the channel.

evidence.snippet: significantly increases current density and hyperpolarizes voltage-dependence of activation by 10 mV, enabling a larger window current
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the shift and the enlarged window current for a disease allele.

evidence.snippet: Nav1.9 exhibited the most hyperpolarized activation, while its fast inactivation resembled the depolarized inactivation of Nav1.8
evidence.explanation: Establishes the wild-type baseline that the disease variants shift further, from a systematic comparison across nine channel subtypes.

steps/4.description: The mutant channel opens at more negative potentials than wild type and carries a larger persistent or window current, so more channels are open near the resting potential. This is the whole biophysical lesion; everything downstream follows from it.

evidence.snippet: Current-clamp recordings in DRG neurons shows that N816K channels depolarize RMP of small DRG neurons by 7 mV
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the resting-potential shift in the relevant neuron type.

evidence.snippet: Nav1.9, as it produces large persistent currents, is attributed a role in determining the resting membrane potential
evidence.explanation: Establishes why this channel, and not another sodium channel, is the one that moves the resting potential.

steps/5.description: Small-diameter dorsal root ganglion neurons sit closer to threshold than they should. NaV1.9 is the channel that normally sets this potential, which is why a gating change in it moves the resting potential rather than the action potential upstroke.

evidence.snippet: Electrophysiological studies using dorsal ganglion neurons showed significant increase of input impedance and firing frequency of evoked action potentials in p.R222S mice
evidence.explanation: Measures the hyperexcitability directly in a knock-in model of a disease allele.

evidence.snippet: cause cold-resistant hyperexcitability of nociceptors, suggesting a mechanistic basis for the temperature dependence of the pain phenotype
evidence.explanation: Establishes the cold-resistant character of the hyperexcitability, which is what ties the cellular defect to the clinical trigger.

steps/6.description: Nociceptors fire action potentials at lower stimulus intensities and at higher frequencies. Crucially the hyperexcitability persists at cold temperatures, where normal nociceptor firing is suppressed - which is the cellular explanation for a pain syndrome that is triggered by cold.

evidence.snippet: here we report a new Nav1.9 mutation, N816K, in a child with early-onset episodic pain in both legs, episodic abdominal pain, and chronic constipation
evidence.explanation: The single reported case establishing the enteric branch.

evidence.snippet: the voltage-gated sodium channel subtype NaV1.9 is expressed in half of gut-projecting rodent dorsal root ganglia sensory neurons
evidence.explanation: Supports gut-projecting expression of the channel in a model system, which is the basis for expecting a visceral branch at all.

steps/7.description: A variant-dependent branch. NaV1.9 is preferentially expressed in myenteric neurons, and in at least one allele the enteric compartment is affected alongside the limbs, producing episodic abdominal pain and chronic constipation. Most reported patients have no gastrointestinal involvement.

evidence.snippet: The affected joints, in an in- creasing order of frequency, include those in the knees, ankles, wrists, and elbows
evidence.explanation: Establishes the distal and lower-limb-predominant distribution.

steps/8.description: Amplified nociceptive traffic from afferents innervating the distal limbs, predominantly the lower limbs. Large-fibre function is spared - nerve conduction studies, imaging and inflammatory markers are normal, and there is no joint pathology - so the acute episode is a signalling abnormality. That does not mean the nerve is structurally intact: a small-fibre lesion is demonstrable on skin biopsy in some patients, and is curated separately as histopathology.

evidence.snippet: Familial episodic pain syndromes (FEPS) are one of the distinctive syndromes characterized by early-childhood onset of severe episodic pain mainly affecting the distal extremities and tend to attenuate or diminish with age
evidence.explanation: States the defining episodic character and its distal distribution.

steps/9.description: Paroxysmal, severe pain lasting fifteen to thirty minutes and recurring several times a day, with complete freedom from pain between episodes. This is the defining feature and is present in essentially all affected individuals.

evidence.snippet: The affected regions feel cold in the patients, and warming the lesions relieves the symptoms
evidence.explanation: Records the cold sensation and the relief by warming, which is the discriminating feature against erythromelalgia.

evidence.snippet: Distal joints, occasionally proximal limbs and neck
evidence.explanation: Gives the fuller distribution, which extends beyond the lower limbs the disease is named for.

steps/10.description: Pain predominantly in the lower limbs, most often the knees and ankles, with the wrists and elbows affected less frequently. The affected region feels cold to the patient and warming it relieves the pain. The distribution is not strictly confined to the legs: the review characterizes FEPS3 pain as affecting distal joints and occasionally the proximal limbs and neck, so the lower-limb predominance in the disease name is a tendency rather than a boundary.

evidence.snippet: The affected joints, in an in- creasing order of frequency, include those in the knees, ankles, wrists, and elbows
evidence.explanation: Gives the joint distribution and its rank order.

steps/11.description: The pain is localized by patients to joints - knees and ankles first, then wrists and elbows - although no joint pathology is present.

evidence.snippet: a child with early-onset episodic pain in both legs, episodic abdominal pain, and chronic constipation
evidence.explanation: The index case for the enteric branch of the phenotype.

steps/12.description: Episodic abdominal pain, reported with the p.Asn816Lys allele and not a feature of most reported patients.

evidence.snippet: episodic pain in both legs, episodic abdominal pain, and chronic constipation
evidence.explanation: Records the constipation in the index case.

steps/13.description: Chronic constipation accompanying the enteric involvement in the same variant.

evidence.snippet: Electrophysiological analysis reveals that p.V1184A shifts the voltage dependence of channel opening to hyperpolarized potentials thereby conferring gain-of-function characteristics to NaV1.9
evidence.explanation: Direct measurement of the gating change caused by the variant.

edges/1.description: The substitution alters channel gating directly, as measured by voltage clamp on the mutant channel.

evidence.snippet: Mutated channels diminish the resting membrane potential of mouse primary sensory neurons and cause cold-resistant hyperexcitability of nociceptors
evidence.explanation: Links the gating change to the resting-potential change in sensory neurons.

edges/2.description: Sustained subthreshold sodium influx near rest shifts the resting potential in the depolarizing direction.

evidence.snippet: reduce current threshold of firing an action potential and render DRG neurons hyperexcitable
evidence.explanation: States the step from resting-potential change to reduced threshold and hyperexcitability.

edges/3.description: A membrane closer to threshold fires on smaller inputs and fires more often.

evidence.snippet: Functional studies have revealed that all missense mutations in these genes are closely associated with the gain-of-function of cation channels
evidence.explanation: Supports the general gain-of-function-to-pain reading across the FEPS genes without demonstrating the intervening step.

edges/4.description: Hyperexcitable afferents are inferred to generate amplified or ectopic nociceptive traffic; the transition from single-neuron excitability to a pain episode has not been recorded in patients.

evidence.snippet: Nav1.9 is preferentially expressed in myenteric neurons, and small-diameter dorsal root ganglion (DRG) and trigeminal ganglion neurons including nociceptors
evidence.explanation: Establishes the expression pattern that makes the enteric branch possible.

edges/5.description: The same channel is preferentially expressed in myenteric neurons, so variants that reach that compartment produce enteric symptoms alongside the limb pain.

evidence.snippet: The pain typically lasts for 15-30 min and recurs several times a day
evidence.explanation: Gives the episode duration and frequency that define the paroxysmal pattern.

edges/6.description: The ectopic afferent traffic is experienced as the paroxysmal pain episode.

evidence.snippet: a child with early-onset episodic pain in both legs, episodic abdominal pain, and chronic constipation
evidence.explanation: Records bilateral leg pain as the presenting complaint.

edges/7.description: The predominant site of the pain, and the feature the disease is named for.

evidence.snippet: The affected joints, in an in- creasing order of frequency, include those in the knees, ankles, wrists, and elbows
evidence.explanation: Records the joint localization without asserting a joint pathology.

edges/8.description: Patients and families localize the pain to joints, though the lesion is in the afferent neuron rather than the joint; whether the perceived joint localization reflects afferent innervation territory is not established.

evidence.snippet: episodic pain in both legs, episodic abdominal pain, and chronic constipation
evidence.explanation: Records the abdominal pain in the index case.

edges/9.description: Hyperexcitable visceral afferents produce episodic abdominal pain.

evidence.snippet: We show that NaV1.9 is required for normal mechanosensation, for direct excitation and for sensitization of mouse colonic afferents
evidence.explanation: Supports a role for the channel in colonic afferent function, from which a motility consequence is inferred rather than shown.

edges/10.description: Constipation accompanies the enteric involvement; whether it follows from altered myenteric motor control or from pain-related behaviour is not established.

evidence.snippet: cause cold-resistant hyperexcitability of nociceptors, suggesting a mechanistic basis for the temperature dependence of the pain phenotype
evidence.explanation: Ties the cold trigger to the cellular mechanism explicitly.

edges/11.description: Cold is the modality at which the mutant channel's hyperexcitability is retained, which is why cooling provokes rather than suppresses firing.

evidence.snippet: The pain is often induced by fa- tigue and is a prelude of bad weather
evidence.explanation: Records fatigue as a trigger, from the clinical description of six families.

edges/12.description: Fatigue is a reproducible clinical trigger, but no mechanism connecting exertion to NaV1.9 activity has been demonstrated.

evidence.snippet: p.R222S and p.R222H, were identified in SCN11A by linkage analysis
evidence.explanation: Gene identification by linkage and exome sequencing in the founding Japanese families.

evidence.snippet: FEPS at least includes four subtypes of FEPS1, FEPS2, FEPS3, and FEPS4, which are caused by mutations in the TRPA1, SCN10A, SCN11A, and SCN9A genes, respectively
evidence.explanation: Places SCN11A as the FEPS3 gene within the four-subtype classification, which is what fixes this entry's scope.

genes/0.notes: Variants are point missense throughout; no frameshift, nonsense or structural variant has been reported for the episodic-pain phenotype, which is consistent with a mechanism that requires an altered channel rather than an absent one. The most instructive fact in the allelic series is that SCN11A is pleiotropic in a graded way: moderate gain of function gives episodic pain, while extreme gain of function gives congenital insensitivity to pain through sustained depolarization block. Leu811 shows this within a single residue.

evidence.snippet: The affected regions feel cold in the patients, and warming the lesions relieves the symptoms
evidence.explanation: The clinical observation that warming relieves the pain.

treatments/0.description: The first-line and most effective intervention: warming the affected limb relieves an episode, and avoiding cold and fatigue reduces episode frequency. It is unusual for a behavioural measure to be first-line, and it follows directly from the mechanism - the trigger is the cold-resistant hyperexcitability, so removing the cold removes the drive.

evidence.snippet: The affected regions feel cold in the patients, and warming the lesions relieves the symptoms
evidence.explanation: Reports symptomatic relief by warming in the founding families.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Warming removes the thermal condition under which the mutant channel sustains firing.

evidence.snippet: This variant was confirmed in other affected members but not in the unaffected father
evidence.explanation: Illustrates the familial segregation testing that cascade counselling rests on.

treatments/1.description: Counselling for the fifty percent recurrence risk of an autosomal dominant condition, with cascade testing of at-risk relatives once a familial variant is known. Counselling can be unusually reassuring here, because the natural history is benign and remits with age.

evidence.snippet: we propose a model in which the physiological consequence of a mutation, that is, augmented versus absent pain, is critically dependent on the type of NaV1.9 hyperactivity
evidence.explanation: States the proposal as a model rather than a demonstrated threshold, which is precisely the gap.

evidence.snippet: Thus, we speculate that p.Leu811Phe may lead to current leakage, while p.Leu811Pro can increase the current through Nav1.9
evidence.explanation: The authors' own hedging ("we speculate") shows the divergence is not yet mechanistically settled even for the one residue where both phenotypes are observed.

open_questions/0.rationale: Both phenotypes arise from gain of function in the same channel, and at Leu811 they arise from different substitutions of the same residue. The proposed explanation is that moderate gain of function lowers the firing threshold while extreme gain of function depolarizes the membrane far enough to inactivate the sodium channels needed to fire at all. No study has measured a quantitative boundary between the two regimes, so a novel variant with demonstrated gain of function cannot yet be assigned to a phenotype on biophysics alone. This matters clinically because the two conditions have opposite management.

evidence.snippet: Affected participants were characterized by infantile recurrent pain episodes, with spontaneous mitigation around adolescence
evidence.explanation: Establishes the phenomenon that lacks a demonstrated mechanism.

evidence.snippet: long-term dysfunction of the Nav1.9 channel may cause degeneration of the unmyelinated fibers in FEPS3 patient with pain remission
evidence.explanation: The one candidate mechanism the literature offers for the remission, hedged by its own authors as a possibility rather than a finding.

open_questions/1.rationale: The remission is the most clinically important fact about this disease - it is why the prognosis is benign - and no mechanism has been demonstrated. The germline variant does not change, so the attenuation must come from something acquired or developmental: changing NaV1.9 expression, changing nociceptor properties, or changing central processing. A fourth candidate is proposed in the literature and is the most uncomfortable one, because it makes the good news and the bad news the same event: long-term NaV1.9 dysfunction may itself degenerate the unmyelinated fibres, so pain could remit because the fibres carrying it are being lost. That would tie this gap directly to the small-fibre histopathology curated in this entry. It is offered speculatively by its authors and has not been measured across the relevant age range in patients, nor in the knock-in mice, which are studied at six to eight weeks.

evidence.snippet:
AVED patients have an 
impaired ability to incorporate alpha-tocopherol into lipoproteins secreted by 
the liver, a function putatively attributable to the alpha-tocopherol transfer 
protein (alpha-TTP).
evidence.explanation: Identifies the core molecular lesion: impaired hepatic incorporation of alpha-tocopherol into secreted lipoproteins due to alpha-TTP.

evidence.snippet:
Here we report the identification of three frame-shift

evidence.explanation: Loss-of-function (frameshift) TTPA mutations underlie the alpha-TTP deficiency.

steps/0.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in TTPA abolish hepatic alpha-tocopherol transfer protein (alpha-TTP) activity. Alpha-TTP normally selects and transfers RRR-alpha-tocopherol within hepatocytes for incorporation into nascent very-low-density lipoprotein (VLDL); without functional alpha-TTP, alpha-tocopherol is not retained or re-secreted into plasma lipoproteins and is instead excreted, so dietary vitamin E cannot reach peripheral tissues.

evidence.snippet:
AVED is 
associated with low plasma vitamin E levels, which results in compromised 
antioxidant function.
evidence.explanation: Confirms low plasma vitamin E and the resulting loss of antioxidant capacity as the central biochemical consequence.

evidence.snippet:
AVED patients have progressive 
spinocerebellar symptoms and markedly reduced plasma levels of vitamin E.
evidence.explanation: An Italian patient series confirms markedly reduced plasma vitamin E as the biochemical hallmark accompanying progressive spinocerebellar disease.

steps/1.description: Because alpha-tocopherol cannot be incorporated into plasma lipoproteins, serum vitamin E concentrations fall to very low levels despite normal dietary intake and normal intestinal absorption. Vitamin E is the major lipid-soluble chain-breaking antioxidant; its systemic depletion is the proximate biochemical hallmark of AVED and distinguishes it from malabsorption causes of vitamin E deficiency.

evidence.snippet:
Dysregulation of this lipid-soluble antioxidant vitamin 
plays a major role in the neurodegeneration observed in AVED.
evidence.explanation: Attributes AVED neurodegeneration to dysregulation of the lipid-soluble antioxidant vitamin E (oxidative mechanism).

evidence.snippet:
is a rare autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disease 
characterized clinically by symptoms with often striking resemblance to those of 
Friedreich ataxia.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the Friedreich-ataxia-like spinocerebellar neurodegenerative phenotype.

steps/2.description: Loss of the lipid-soluble antioxidant vitamin E leaves neuronal and axonal membranes unprotected against lipid peroxidation and reactive oxygen species. Large-caliber myelinated sensory neurons of the dorsal root ganglia, the posterior columns (dorsal columns), and cerebellar pathways are preferentially vulnerable, producing the spinocerebellar degeneration that clinically resembles Friedreich ataxia.

treatments/0.description: Lifelong high-dose oral vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol) supplementation is the disease-modifying targeted therapy for AVED, dosed to bring plasma vitamin E into the high-normal range. Initiated in presymptomatic individuals it prevents disease manifestations; started early in symptomatic patients it can partially reverse ataxia and mental deterioration, though neurologic recovery is often slow and incomplete.

evidence.snippet: Multi-omics analysis of mouse Plaat3-/- and patient-derived WAT showed enrichment of arachidonic acid-containing membrane phospholipids and a strong decrease in the signaling of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ), the master regulator of adipocyte differentiation.
evidence.explanation: Patient-derived white adipose tissue shows both the phospholipid remodeling and the fall in PPARgamma signaling that this node and its downstream edge assert.

evidence.snippet: CRISPR-Cas9-mediated PLAAT3 inactivation in human adipose stem cells induced insulin resistance, altered adipocyte differentiation with decreased lipid droplet formation and reduced the expression of adipogenic and mature adipocyte markers, including PPARγ.
evidence.explanation: Directed inactivation in human adipose stem cells reproduces the differentiation defect, establishing the direction of the link rather than only its correlation.

steps/6.description: PLAAT3 is a phospholipid-modifying enzyme expressed in neural tissue and white adipose tissue. Biallelic loss of function enriches white adipose membranes in arachidonic-acid-containing phospholipids and strongly lowers PPARgamma signaling, so the lesion is upstream of the adipogenic transcriptional program rather than in it. This is the FPLD9 route.

evidence.snippet: PPARγ plays an essential role in adipogenesis, stimulating the differentiation of preadipocytes into adipocytes. Loss-of-function pathogenic variants in PPARG reduce the activity of the PPARγ receptor and can lead to severe metabolic consequences associated with familial partial lipodystrophy type 3 (FPLD3).
evidence.explanation: States both the adipogenic role of PPARgamma and the reduction of receptor activity by loss-of-function PPARG variants that this node asserts.

steps/7.description: PPARgamma is the master transcriptional regulator of preadipocyte-to-adipocyte differentiation. Two curated routes converge on reduced PPARgamma signaling: loss-of-function PPARG variants themselves (FPLD3), and biallelic PLAAT3 loss (FPLD9), which remodels white adipose membrane phospholipids and strongly lowers PPARgamma signaling without altering PPARG itself.

evidence.snippet: The mechanism of pathogenicity is reported to be loss of function, evidenced by in vitro functional assays showed that the AKT2 Arg274His allele has little or no kinase activity.
evidence.explanation: ClinGen's mechanistic review records the kinase-dead behaviour of the reported allele, the molecular basis of this node.

evidence.snippet: AKT2 signaling is also important for adipocyte differentiation
evidence.explanation: Links the signaling defect to the adipocyte differentiation failure this node feeds.

steps/8.description: AKT2 is a kinase of the insulin/PI3K-AKT pathway, and ClinGen's review of the reported evidence records that AKT2 signaling is important for adipocyte differentiation. The reported FPLD allele has little or no kinase activity, so insulin signaling fails in the adipocyte itself rather than only downstream of an adipose deficit.

evidence.snippet: Research on laminopathies has highlighted how LMNA mutations disrupt adipose tissue function and metabolic regulation, leading to altered fat distribution and metabolic pathway dysfunctions.
evidence.explanation: Supports LMNA-driven disruption of adipose tissue function and metabolic regulation as the FPLD2 mechanism.

steps/9.description: In FPLD2 (Dunnigan), pathogenic LMNA variants (commonly codon 482) perturb lamin A/C structure and lamin-chromatin (lamina-associated domain) interactions required for adipocyte differentiation and maintenance, with suppression of lipid-metabolism and mitochondrial programs and an intrinsic inflammatory transcriptional signature. (Adipocyte-specific Lmna-knockout mouse data supporting a cell-autonomous role for lamin A/C in adipocyte maintenance are summarized in the entry notes.)

evidence.snippet: In addition to describing a novel autosomal recessive form of familial partial lipodystrophy, these observations also suggest that CIDEC is required for unilocular lipid droplet formation and optimal energy storage in human fat.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the unilocular-droplet requirement whose failure is the CIDEC arm of this node.

evidence.snippet: Mechanistic studies suggest that subcutaneous patients’ adipose tissues show reduced full-length perilipin-1 and an extended perilipin-1 form compatible with the predicted elongated C-terminal tail of the mutant proteins
evidence.explanation: ClinGen's mechanistic review records the altered perilipin-1 protein on the droplet in patient adipose tissue, which is the PLIN1 arm of this node.

steps/10.description: CIDEC and PLIN1 act at the adipocyte lipid droplet itself. CIDEC is required for unilocular lipid droplet formation and for optimal energy storage in human fat; the truncating allele is mistargeted and fails to increase lipid droplet size, and the patient's white adipocytes are multiloculated (FPLD5). PLIN1 coats the droplet, and the FPLD4 frameshift alleles extend its C-terminus and act dominant-negatively rather than by haploinsufficiency.

evidence.snippet: the p.(Val398Glyfs) and p.(Leu404Alafs) mutants fail to interact with ABHD5, leading to constitutive activation of adipocyte triglyceride lipase
evidence.explanation: Gives the molecular route from the FPLD4 perilipin-1 alleles to unchecked lipolysis asserted in this node.

evidence.snippet: ADRA2A is the main presynaptic inhibitory feedback G protein-coupled receptor regulating norepinephrine release. Activation of ADRA2A inhibits cAMP production and reduces lipolysis in adipocytes.
evidence.explanation: States the normal restraining role of ADRA2A on adipocyte lipolysis that the reported loss-of-function variant removes.

evidence.snippet: the mutant ADRA2A produced more cAMP and glycerol, which were resistant to the effects of the α2-adrenergic receptor agonist clonidine and the α2-adrenergic receptor antagonist yohimbine, suggesting loss of function.
evidence.explanation: Cell assays show the mutant receptor raises cAMP and glycerol release, the functional signature of increased lipolysis in this node.

steps/11.description: Three curated genes disturb the release of stored triglyceride from the adipocyte droplet, in opposite directions, which is why the node is tagged abnormal rather than increased or decreased. PLIN1 frameshift mutants fail to hold ABHD5, so adipose triglyceride lipase is constitutively activated and basal lipolysis runs unchecked (FPLD4). The reported ADRA2A variant removes the presynaptic alpha-2A adrenergic brake on adipocyte cAMP, again raising lipolysis, and is proposed to do so only in some depots (FPLD8). LIPE encodes hormone-sensitive lipase itself, so biallelic loss instead impairs triglyceride mobilization (FPLD6).

evidence.snippet: All variants were clustered in the heterodimerization domain of the negative regulatory region of NOTCH3.
evidence.explanation: Localizes the reported variants to the domain that normally restrains receptor activation, which is the basis for calling the effect a gain of function rather than a quantitative increase.

evidence.snippet: RNA sequencing and proteomics analysis of skin fibroblasts revealed significantly higher RNA and protein expression of NOTCH3 and activation of widespread senescence pathways in the patients with FPL versus control study participants.
evidence.explanation: Patient-derived fibroblasts carry both halves of this node, raised NOTCH3 expression and activated senescence programs.

steps/12.description: Missense variants clustered in the heterodimerization domain of the NOTCH3 negative regulatory region were reported in three unrelated FPL families. Patient skin fibroblasts show raised NOTCH3 RNA and protein and activation of widespread senescence pathways, which the authors propose as the route from unrestrained NOTCH3 signaling to loss of adipose tissue. This node records a single-publication mechanism; see the notes on the NOTCH3 genetic record.

evidence.snippet: PPARγ plays an essential role in adipogenesis, stimulating the differentiation of preadipocytes into adipocytes. Loss-of-function pathogenic variants in PPARG reduce the activity of the PPARγ receptor and can lead to severe metabolic consequences associated with familial partial lipodystrophy type 3 (FPLD3).
evidence.explanation: Establishes impaired adipogenesis (via PPARgamma loss of function) as a core mechanism producing the lipodystrophy and metabolic phenotype.

steps/13.description: The unifying defect across FPLD subtypes is failure of subcutaneous adipose tissue to develop and/or store triglycerides normally, owing to disruption of adipogenesis, lipid-droplet biology, or adipocyte maintenance. This produces selective loss of subcutaneous fat from the limbs and gluteal region.

evidence.snippet: their associated metabolic complications, such as insulin resistance, hypertriglyceridemia, hepatic steatosis, and metabolic syndrome, all of which elevate the risk of cardiovascular disease, stroke, and diabetes.
evidence.explanation: Supports the downstream cascade of insulin resistance, hypertriglyceridemia, hepatic steatosis, and cardiovascular risk arising from adipose dysfunction.

steps/14.description: The limited subcutaneous storage capacity forces triglycerides into ectopic sites (liver, muscle, viscera), driving severe insulin resistance, hypertriglyceridemia, type 2 diabetes, hepatic steatosis, and downstream cardiometabolic disease.

edges/7.description: Reduced subcutaneous storage capacity diverts lipid to ectopic sites, driving systemic insulin resistance.

edges/8.description: LMNA-driven adipose dysfunction feeds the shared ectopic-lipid and insulin-resistance cascade.

edges/9.description: Reduced PPARgamma transcriptional output blocks preadipocyte differentiation, limiting the subcutaneous adipose compartment that can be built and maintained.

edges/10.description: Phospholipid remodeling of white adipose membranes lowers PPARgamma signaling, joining the FPLD3 route at the adipogenic transcription node.

edges/11.description: Adipocytes that cannot build or coat a normal unilocular droplet store triglyceride inefficiently, reducing safe subcutaneous storage capacity.

edges/12.description: The same droplet-coat defect removes the perilipin-1 brake on lipase access to stored triglyceride.

edges/13.description: Triglyceride that cannot be retained in, or mobilized from, subcutaneous adipocytes reaches ectopic depots.

edges/14.description: Loss of AKT2 kinase output impairs the insulin-driven differentiation and storage program of the adipocyte.

edges/15.description: A kinase-dead AKT2 also blocks insulin action directly, so the insulin resistance is not solely a consequence of reduced fat mass.

edges/16.description: Senescence activation is the proposed route by which unrestrained NOTCH3 signaling depletes the subcutaneous adipose compartment.

The mechanism is dominant-negative rather than haploinsufficient: ClinGen's review of the reported alleles records that only frameshift variants extending the perilipin-1 C-terminus have been implicated in humans, and that heterozygous null variants predicted to undergo nonsense-mediated decay are not associated with FPLD4.

evidence.snippet: we describe a female patient with partial lipodystrophy (affecting limb, femorogluteal and subcutaneous abdominal fat), white adipocytes with multiloculated lipid droplets and insulin-resistant diabetes, who was found to be homozygous for a premature truncation mutation in the lipid droplet protein cell death-inducing Dffa-like effector C (CIDEC) (E186X).
evidence.explanation: The founding report of biallelic CIDEC loss of function in human partial lipodystrophy, including the multilocular-lipid-droplet adipocyte phenotype that distinguishes this subtype.

genes/3.notes: Biallelic CIDEC variants cause autosomal recessive FPLD5, impairing lipid-droplet formation and lipid storage. The founding report is a single homozygous proband with supporting cell and mouse work. No ClinGen gene-disease validity curation exists for CIDEC: the ClinGen validity table committed in this repository (cache/clingen/gene_validity.csv) contains no CIDEC row, so the CAUSATIVE relationship_type rests on the primary report and on OMIM/MONDO recognition of the locus rather than on a ClinGen classification.

genes/4.notes: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in LIPE (hormone-sensitive lipase) cause autosomal recessive FPLD6.

evidence.snippet: AKT2 | HGNC:392 | AKT2-related familial partial lipodystrophy | MONDO:0019192 | AD | Limited
evidence.explanation: ClinGen classifies the AKT2-FPLD relationship as Limited, which is the evidence level this record reports.

evidence.snippet: In summary, while the mechanistic link between AKT2 dysfunction and lipodystrophic insulin resistance is highly plausible and well evidenced, current genetic evidence supporting the human gene-disease relationship is limited.
evidence.explanation: Distinguishes the strong mechanistic case for AKT2 from the limited human genetic evidence, which is why relationship_type is left UNKNOWN here.

genes/5.notes: Dominant-negative variants in AKT2, a kinase in the insulin/PI3K-AKT pathway, cause partial lipodystrophy with severe insulin resistance. ClinGen rates this gene-disease relationship Limited: the mechanism is well evidenced but the human genetic evidence still rests on one kindred. relationship_type is UNKNOWN rather than CAUSATIVE because GeneDiseaseRelationshipEnum defines CAUSATIVE as ClinGen Definitive or Strong and has no Limited value; it is not DISPUTED, because nothing contradicts the association.

evidence.snippet: CAV1 | HGNC:1527 | lipodystrophy | MONDO:0006573 | AD | Limited
evidence.explanation: ClinGen classifies the autosomal dominant CAV1-lipodystrophy relationship as Limited, the evidence level this record reports.

evidence.snippet: Evidence supporting this gene-disease relationship includes limited case-level data, with no segregation data or experimental data available.
evidence.explanation: States what the CAV1 partial-lipodystrophy claim rests on, supporting the caution recorded in this record's notes.

genes/6.notes: Variants in CAV1 (caveolin-1) are associated with partial lipodystrophy (FPLD7, OMIM 606721), affecting adipocyte caveolae and lipid storage. ClinGen rates this Limited: only two variants from a single 2008 publication have been reported, with no segregation or experimental data. ClinGen split CAV1 into three curations - the autosomal dominant partial and/or progeroid lipodystrophy curated here, autosomal recessive congenital generalized lipodystrophy type 3 (OMIM 612526, rated Definitive; curated in dismech as the CGL3 subtype of kb/disorders/Berardinelli_Seip_Congenital_Lipodystrophy.yaml), and autosomal dominant pulmonary arterial hypertension - so a CAV1 result must be read against the right one of the three. relationship_type is UNKNOWN for the same enum reason given on the AKT2 record.
