treatments/5.description: A loop diuretic used adjunctively in some centres. A retrospective cohort of 273 HAPE inpatients found lower CT severity scores with furosemide, but the evidence is observational and its effect on outcome is unestablished; it is not a substitute for descent or oxygen.

treatments/5/targets/0.description: Diuresis reduces pulmonary vascular filling pressure and total lung water, acting on the accumulated edema rather than its cause.

hypotheses/0.description: HAPE begins as a hemodynamic disease: exaggerated, uneven hypoxic vasoconstriction raises pulmonary capillary pressure past the mechanical tolerance of the blood-gas barrier, and inflammation follows the resulting stress failure. The decisive evidence is that transcapillary protein escape is still normal in susceptible subjects whose capillary pressure has already risen, and that agents which lower pulmonary artery pressure prevent the disease while anti-inflammatory action alone does not account for the benefit.

hypotheses/1.description: A minority view holds that immune dysregulation contributes to the initiation of barrier failure rather than merely amplifying it, supported by elevated IL-2, IL-10, and TNF in HAPE patients and by cytokine profiles that discriminate cases from acclimatized controls with high accuracy. The unresolved problem is temporal: the human cytokine data are cross-sectional in established disease and cannot separate cause from consequence, and lavage inflammation appears after the pressure rise in the studies that measured both.

open_questions/0.rationale: Susceptibility is reproducible within individuals and is the single largest determinant of who develops HAPE, yet prophylaxis is currently offered on the basis of prior episodes rather than any prospective measurement. Enhanced hypoxic vasoreactivity is already detectable at low altitude in susceptible subjects, so a predictive test is physiologically plausible; what is missing is a validated threshold and an understanding of what sets the reactivity.

open_questions/1.rationale: The chip reproduces hypoxia-driven barrier protein loss and responds to perfluorocarbon, but it has no pulmonary circulation and therefore cannot generate the uneven vasoconstriction and regional capillary hypertension that the human evidence identifies as the initiating lesion. The mismatch matters because a therapeutic that works by protecting the barrier against direct hypoxic injury need not work against a mechanically overloaded barrier. A chip incorporating controllable perfusion pressure across a capillary network would test whether the same protection holds when the insult is hemodynamic.

evidence.snippet: Whole-exome and -genome sequencing revealed a de novo c.2144A>G variant in CLCN7 in both affected children.
evidence.explanation: The human-genetics half of this node's claim: the variant exists, is de novo, and was found in patients. Split from the electrophysiology below, which is a different kind of study reported in the same paper.

evidence.snippet: This p.Tyr715Cys variant, located in the C-terminal domain of ClC-7, resulted in increased outward currents when it was heterologously expressed in Xenopus oocytes.
evidence.explanation: Locates the substitution in the C-terminal domain and establishes that it increases current. Heterologous expression in Xenopus oocytes is an in-vitro measurement, so this is IN_VITRO even though the paper as a whole is a patient study.

steps/1.description: Two variants have been reported: p.Tyr715Cys (c.2144A>G), carried by four of the five published patients, and p.Lys285Thr (c.854A>C) in one. Both lie in the cytoplasmic portion of ClC-7 and affect residues lining the binding pocket for the signalling lipid PI(3,5)P2, which is the point of convergence between two otherwise distant substitutions.

steps/2.description: PI(3,5)P2 normally restrains ClC-7. Both HOD variants weaken that restraint and shift voltage-dependent gating toward less positive potentials, so more of the transporter population is open at physiological membrane voltages.

evidence.snippet: This shift predicts augmented pH gradient-driven Cl- uptake into vesicles.
evidence.explanation: States the transport consequence of the gating shift.

steps/3.description: The functional lesion. Heterologous expression of p.Tyr715Cys yields increased outward currents, and the gating shift is predicted to drive extra chloride into the vesicle lumen down the existing pH gradient.

evidence.snippet: Our results show that p.Tyr715Cys is a gain-of-function CLCN7 variant associated with developmental delay, organomegaly, and hypopigmentation resulting from lysosomal hyperacidity, abnormal storage, and enlarged intracellular vacuoles.
evidence.explanation: The authors' summary statement of the mechanism, naming hyperacidity as causal.

steps/4.description: Patient fibroblasts sit about 0.2 pH units below control. The size of that shift is worth stating plainly: it is small in absolute terms, and it is the disease. Note the direction, because it is the opposite of the intuition carried over from most lysosomal storage disorders, where the lysosome fails to acidify.

evidence.snippet: Primary fibroblasts from both probands also exhibited markedly enlarged intracellular vacuoles; this finding was recapitulated by the overexpression of human p.Tyr715Cys CLCN7 in control fibroblasts, reflecting the dominant, gain-of-function nature of the variant.
evidence.explanation: Shows the vacuoles in patient cells and reproduces them in control cells by expressing the variant, which is what makes the variant causal rather than correlated.

evidence.snippet: Overactivity of ClC-7 induces pathologically enlarged vacuoles in many tissues, which is distinct from lysosomal storage observed with the loss of ClC-7 function.
evidence.explanation: Distinguishes the gain-of-function cellular lesion from the loss-of-function one.

evidence.snippet: Bafilomycin treatment abrogated vacuole generation, indicating that H+-driven Cl- accumulation osmotically drives vesicle enlargement.
evidence.explanation: Supplies the physical mechanism this node otherwise states without explaining - the vesicles swell because chloride is osmotically dragged in behind pumped protons. It is INDIRECT because it was shown for the sibling exchanger ClC-6, not ClC-7. The parallel is close: a de novo gain-of-function substitution in an endolysosomal CLC, slowed gating, larger currents, giant vacuoles requiring intact Cl-/H+ exchange.

steps/5.description: Grossly enlarged vacuoles arise by membrane fusion and are seen in patient fibroblasts, leukocytes, liver and kidney. This is the feature that distinguishes gain of ClC-7 function from its loss: losing ClC-7 also produces storage, but not these vacuoles.

evidence.snippet: In cells expressing the ClC-7 gain-of-function mutant, autophagic clearance was largely impaired, resulting in a build-up of autophagic material.
evidence.explanation: Directly reports the autophagic block in cells carrying the HOD variant.

evidence.snippet: Degradation of endocytosed material was reduced in these compartments and resulted in an accumulation of lysosomal storage material.
evidence.explanation: Links the enlarged compartments to failed degradation and to storage.

steps/6.description: Degradation of endocytosed material falls inside the enlarged compartments and autophagic clearance is largely blocked, so undegraded substrate accumulates.

evidence.snippet: The activity of tyrosinase, the rate-limiting enzyme required for melanin synthesis, is generally minimal in an acidic environment.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the pH dependence of tyrosinase in melanocytes. It is about vitamin-C-driven cytoplasmic acidification, not ClC-7, so it supports the step by inference rather than by observation in this disease.

evidence.snippet: Numerous studies have shown that the pH of melanosome plays a key role in the regulation of melanin synthesis.
evidence.explanation: Independent support that melanosomal pH governs pigment output. Again general melanocyte biology, not a measurement in HOD syndrome.

steps/7.description: The proposed route to hypopigmentation, and the weakest link in this entry's chain. The melanosome is a lysosome-related organelle, tyrosinase is the rate-limiting enzyme of melanin synthesis and is inhibited at acidic pH, so a transporter that over-acidifies lysosomes is expected to over-acidify melanosomes and suppress pigment. Every step of that is plausible and none of it has been measured in this disease: no study has reported melanosomal pH, tyrosinase activity or melanosome morphology in a patient with HOD syndrome. The supporting evidence below is drawn from melanocyte biology generally and is marked INDIRECT for that reason.

evidence.snippet: A liver biopsy taken at 19 months of age revealed numerous CD68+ histiocytic cells, particularly in the portal fields, with foamy, highly expanded, and light-colored cytoplasm.
evidence.explanation: Histological demonstration of foam-cell transformation in a patient.

steps/8.description: Tissue macrophages fill with undegraded material and become foam cells, most heavily in liver portal fields and renal medullary interstitium. The organs enlarge while their function is preserved, which is an unusual combination and a useful diagnostic clue.

evidence.snippet: Both children had delayed myelination and development, organomegaly, and hypopigmentation, but neither had osteopetrosis.
evidence.explanation: Records delayed myelination and development in the index patients.

evidence.snippet: A cranial MRI at 14 months of age revealed delayed myelination in addition to reduced cerebral volume, particularly evident in the frontotemporal region.
evidence.explanation: Radiological confirmation with the additional finding of volume loss.

steps/9.description: Delayed myelination on MRI, and in the longest-followed patient reduced cerebral volume with frontotemporal accentuation and symmetrical signal change in the subthalamic nuclei. Split from the developmental phenotype below: both follow the lysosomal lesion, but no source establishes that the myelination delay is what causes the developmental delay, so no edge is drawn between them.

evidence.snippet: Note hypopigmentation of hair including eyebrows but not the irides, the massively distended abdomen due to organomegaly, and a gastric tube in place because of impaired intestinal transit.
evidence.explanation: Records the distribution of the pigment defect, including the sparing of the irides that separates it from classical oculocutaneous albinism.

steps/10.description: Present in all five reported patients. In the best-described case the hair and eyebrows are hypopigmented while the irides are not, so this is not uniform oculocutaneous albinism.

evidence.snippet: Both children had delayed myelination and development, organomegaly, and hypopigmentation, but neither had osteopetrosis.
evidence.explanation: Records organomegaly in the two index patients alongside the absence of bone disease.

evidence.snippet: Over time, he also developed grossly enlarged organs with fully preserved function (liver, spleen, and kidneys).
evidence.explanation: The preserved-function detail matters clinically - it means normal liver and renal panels do not argue against the diagnosis.

steps/11.description: Liver, spleen and kidneys enlarge, in one case to the point of a massively distended abdomen, while laboratory function of those organs stays normal.

evidence.snippet: The clinical picture is dominated by progressive thickening of bowel walls, resulting in chronic impairment of intestinal transit, an extremely distended abdomen, malabsorption, loss of protein and electrolytes, and failure to thrive
evidence.explanation: Establishes the enteropathy and its weight in the overall clinical picture.

steps/12.description: Progressive bowel-wall thickening impairs intestinal transit, with malabsorption and loss of protein and electrolytes. In the most fully reported patient this, rather than the neurological disease, dominates the clinical course.

evidence.snippet: The clinical picture is dominated by progressive thickening of bowel walls, resulting in chronic impairment of intestinal transit, an extremely distended abdomen, malabsorption, loss of protein and electrolytes, and failure to thrive
evidence.explanation: The same sentence cited on the enteropathy node, quoted whole here too. The earlier form was the trailing noun phrase alone, which asserted nothing and left the causal reading resting on word order; this version carries the claim that the growth failure follows the enteric losses.

steps/13.description: Growth failure downstream of the enteric losses rather than of poor intake. Split from the enteropathy node so the causal step between them is explicit rather than bundled.

evidence.snippet: We clinically and genetically evaluated a Taiwanese boy presenting with developmental delay, organomegaly, hypogammaglobulinemia and hypopigmentation without osteopetrosis.
evidence.explanation: The fifth reported patient.

steps/14.description: 5/5 published patients. As with hypopigmentation, this is one of the features the syndrome is defined by.

evidence.snippet: Both mutations decreased ClC-7 inhibition by PI(3,5)P2 and affected residues lining its binding pocket
evidence.explanation: States that the variants act by removing lipid inhibition of the transporter.

edges/1.description: Both reported variants sit in or beside the PI(3,5)P2 binding pocket.

evidence.snippet: Loss of PI(3,5)P2 inhibition will further increase current amplitudes, but may not be a general feature of HOD.
evidence.explanation: Supports the link while recording the authors' own limit on it - they attribute the gain principally to the gating shift and treat lost lipid inhibition as additive.

evidence.snippet: Knock-out of CLCN7 corrected lysosomal swelling and partially corrected lysosomal hyperacidification in FIG4 null cell cultures.
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation of this step from the opposite direction. FIG4 loss lowers PI(3,5)P2 and so removes the same inhibition of ClC-7, producing enlarged and over-acidified lysosomes - and deleting CLCN7 reverses both. That is the HOD lesion arrived at through a different gene, which is why it is INDIRECT here.

evidence.snippet: Fibroblasts from probands displayed a lysosomal pH approximately 0.2 units lower than that of control cells, and treatment with chloroquine normalized the pH.
evidence.explanation: Measures the pH consequence in patient cells and shows it is reversible by an alkalinizing agent, which is what ties the pH shift to transporter activity.

evidence.snippet: increased ClC-7 Cl-/H+ exchange activity is required for the formation of enlarged vacuoles by membrane fusion
evidence.explanation: Uncoupling mutations separate transport from the phenotype and show the exchange activity is necessary for vacuole formation.

edges/4.description: A second, partly separable consequence - vacuole formation was shown to require the exchange activity itself, not merely the acidification it produces.

edges/6.description: Proposed rather than measured in this disease. See the knowledge gap attached to this edge - no study has recorded melanosomal pH in a patient with HOD syndrome.

edges/10.description: Restores the link that the myelination/development split dropped. Held to the same standard as the myelination edge beside it - both outcomes follow the lysosomal lesion, and the intermediates are unknown for each. This is deliberately not routed through Delayed Myelination, because no source establishes that the myelination delay is what causes the developmental delay.

edges/14.description: The enteric losses are what the growth failure is attributed to.

evidence.snippet: Whole-exome sequencing revealed a de novo gain-of-function variant, p.Tyr715Cys, in the C-terminal domain of ClC-7 encoded by CLCN7.
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation of the recurrent de novo gain-of-function variant.

evidence.snippet: This variant is absent in the gnomAD database (v.4.0) and is predicted to be deleterious by various commonly applied bioinformatics prediction programs with a CADD score of 28.6 and a REVEL score of 0.872.
evidence.explanation: Population-frequency and in-silico support for the second, novel variant p.Lys285Thr.

evidence.snippet: it seems that ADO II reflects a dominant negative effect, whereas loss-of-function mutations in ClCN7 do not cause abnormalities in heterozygous individuals
evidence.explanation: Source for the allelic architecture above, and specifically for the claim that heterozygous loss of CLCN7 is silent - which is what makes the dominant-negative and gain-of-function alleles the only heterozygous routes to disease.

genes/0.notes:
CLCN7 encodes ClC-7, which with its obligatory beta-subunit OSTM1 performs 2Cl-/H+ exchange across the lysosomal membrane and across the osteoclast ruffled border. Four allelic outcomes are on record, and they do not lie on a single dose axis:
biallelic loss of function causes infantile malignant autosomal recessive osteopetrosis; a dominant-negative allele causes Albers-Schonberg autosomal dominant osteopetrosis type II; the gain-of-function alleles below cause HOD syndrome with no bone phenotype at all; and simple heterozygous loss of function causes no abnormality whatever. That last point is the one most easily lost - CLCN7 haploinsufficiency is silent, so ADO II is not "half of" recessive osteopetrosis, and HOD is not the far end of a severity gradient.

evidence.snippet: Fibroblasts from probands displayed a lysosomal pH approximately 0.2 units lower than that of control cells, and treatment with chloroquine normalized the pH.
evidence.explanation: Chloroquine corrects the primary biochemical lesion in patient cells. This is a claim about mechanism, in fibroblasts.

evidence.snippet: clinical course is progressive despite treatment with chloroquine, a drug known to increase lysosomal pH
evidence.explanation: Refutes clinical benefit in the one patient followed on treatment. A separate claim from the in-vitro rescue above, and the one that matters for care.

treatments/0.description: The only mechanism-directed treatment tried. Chloroquine is lysosomotropic and raises lysosomal pH, so it opposes the primary lesion directly, and in patient fibroblasts it normalised the pH. The clinical result did not follow: one patient treated from 19 months of age continued to progress. The two evidence items below therefore point in opposite directions on purpose - the first supports the mechanism, the second refutes clinical efficacy, and collapsing them into a single graded item would lose exactly the information a clinician needs.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Raises lysosomal pH, opposing the transporter's over-acidification.

evidence.snippet: However, the patient was found to have hypogammaglobulinemia with low serum IgG and IgM immunoglobulin levels, requiring intravenous immunoglobulin replacement treatment to prevent infections.
evidence.explanation: Records the indication and that replacement was actually administered.

treatments/1.description: Given to the one reported patient with hypogammaglobulinemia, to prevent infection. This is supportive rather than mechanism-directed: it replaces the missing product, and does nothing about the transporter. Whether the immunoglobulin deficiency is itself a consequence of the lysosomal lesion is an open question recorded in the discussions.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Replaces the deficient immunoglobulin rather than correcting its cause.

evidence.snippet: The patient exhibited protein‐losing enteropathy that required placement of a percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy tube to provide supplemental nutritional support.
evidence.explanation: Ties the gastrostomy directly to the protein-losing enteropathy node.

treatments/2.description: Percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy for supplemental nutrition, driven by the enteropathy rather than by poor intake. therapeutic_modality is deliberately left unset: the treatment is nutrition delivered through a device, and neither DEVICE nor BEHAVIORAL describes it honestly.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Supports growth against enteric protein and electrolyte loss.

evidence.snippet: Osteopetrosis results from a loss of ClC-7, but osteoclasts remain resilient to increased ClC-7 activity.
evidence.explanation: States the asymmetry without accounting for it, which is the gap.

open_questions/0.rationale: This is the question the disease poses most sharply, and answering it would say something general about how much of ClC-7 physiology is set by the transporter versus by the compartment it sits in. It also has a practical edge: if a therapy for the osteopetroses ever aims to raise ClC-7 activity, the safety question is whether it would reproduce HOD, and the answer currently rests on five patients.

evidence.snippet: The normal coat colour of Clcn7(td/td) mice and their less severe neurodegeneration suggested that the ClC-7 protein, even when lacking measurable ion transport activity, is sufficient for hair pigmentation
evidence.explanation: Sharpens the gap rather than filling it, and cuts against a purely transport-based account of the pigment defect. Mice expressing a transport-dead ClC-7 have normal coat colour, so pigmentation survives the loss of ion transport while depending on the protein being present. Whatever excess transport does to the melanosome in HOD, it is not simply the mirror of losing transport.

open_questions/1.rationale: The melanosome step is the weakest link in this entry's causal chain and the only one supported entirely by evidence from outside the disease. The inference is reasonable - melanosomes are lysosome-related organelles and tyrosinase is pH-sensitive - but it has not been tested, and the knock-in mouse makes it testable. The deep-research report reached the same chain independently and listed the same step among its own limitations.

evidence.snippet: Interestingly, not all osteopetrosis-causing CLCN7 mutations from patients are associated with a loss of ion transport. Some rather result in an acceleration of voltage-dependent ClC-7 activation.
evidence.explanation: Refutes the simple reading that increased ClC-7 activation is sufficient to produce the HOD phenotype rather than osteopetrosis.

open_questions/2.rationale: The tidy summary - gain gives HOD, loss gives osteopetrosis - is the one this entry is built around, and it is not sufficient on its own. Some variants that accelerate voltage-dependent activation nevertheless cause osteopetrosis. Whatever separates them from p.Tyr715Cys and p.Lys285Thr is unknown, and the PI(3,5)P2 binding site is the current candidate because both HOD variants sit in it. Recording this stops the entry asserting a cleaner genotype-phenotype rule than the evidence supports.

evidence.snippet: we show that microglia and embryonic macrophages in zebrafish clcn7 mutants cannot effectively process extracellular debris in the form of apoptotic cells and β-amyloid
evidence.explanation: Cited to mark the boundary of what is known, not as support. This is a loss-of-function zebrafish study, so it establishes that microglia need ClC-7 but says nothing about what excess ClC-7 activity does to them, which is the question HOD raises.

open_questions/3.rationale: Delayed myelination is one of the four features the syndrome is named for, and it is the least mechanistically explained. What is known about ClC-7 in the CNS comes from loss of function, which cannot be assumed to transfer to a gain-of-function disease - the mouse knockout shows that losing ClC-7 produces storage without any pH change at all.

open_questions/4.rationale: The deep-research report proposed a mechanistic immune branch - impaired endolysosomal processing in B cells causing hypogammaglobulinemia. That is a plausible hypothesis and it is recorded here as one, not curated as a causal edge: it rests on a single patient, and no B-cell or immunoglobulin work has been done in this disease. The finding was prominent enough in that report for the case to be framed as an inborn error of immunity, which is exactly why it is worth marking as unestablished.

evidence.snippet: are predicted to truncate the protein, and loss of the major TBCK isoform was confirmed in primary fibroblasts from one affected individual
evidence.explanation: Confirms that the causal alleles truncate TBCK and that the major isoform is lost in patient cells.

evidence.snippet: TBCK was absent in cells from affected individuals
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation that patient cells lack TBCK protein.

steps/1.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous loss-of-function variants in TBCK (nonsense, frameshift, canonical splice-site, and a recurrent single-exon deletion of exon 23) abolish the major TBCK isoform. TBCK protein is absent from patient cells, so the disorder behaves as a complete loss of TBCK function rather than a hypomorphic or dominant-negative state.

evidence.snippet: we identify TBCK as the catalytic core of a heterotrimeric complex comprising TBCK, PPP1R21, and FERRY3/C12orf4. This complex functions as a specific GTPase-activating protein (GAP) for RAB5.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the complex and its RAB5-GAP activity.

evidence.snippet: we find TBCK interacts with PPP1R21, C12orf4, and Cryzl1, consistent with TBCK being part of the FERRY mRNA transport complex
evidence.explanation: Unbiased proteomics in patient-derived human neurons confirms the complex membership in the disease-relevant cell type.

evidence.snippet: Interestingly, three members of the FERRY complex are associated with ultra-rare neurogenetic disorders.
evidence.explanation: Places TBCK loss within a wider FERRY-complex disease class (with PPP1R21 and FERRY3), supporting the complex as the disease-relevant unit.

evidence.snippet: Biochemical and biophysical analyses reveal that the catalytically inactive pseudokinase domain of TBCK lacks nucleotide binding, consistent with the absence of the canonical VAIK, HRD, and DFG motifs required for catalysis.
evidence.explanation: Purified full-length human TBCK shows its N-terminal kinase-like domain is a catalytically inactive class I pseudokinase, so the "kinase" in the gene name is not the disease-relevant activity; the TBC/Rab-GAP domain is.

steps/2.description: TBCK forms a heterotrimer with PPP1R21 and FERRY3/C12orf4 that acts as a specific GTPase-activating protein for RAB5, and is a subunit of the wider five-subunit FERRY complex (with CRYZL1 and GATD1) that couples early endosomes to mRNA for peripheral local translation. Loss of the GAP leaves RAB5 constitutively GTP-bound. Despite the gene name, TBCK's N-terminal kinase-like domain is a catalytically inactive class I pseudokinase lacking the VAIK, HRD and DFG motifs and nucleotide binding, so the disease-relevant activity resides in the central TBC/Rab-GAP domain.

evidence.snippet: decreased phosphorylation of phospho-ribosomal protein S6 was also observed, a finding suggestive of downregulation of mTOR signaling
evidence.explanation: The primary observation of reduced mTORC1 output in patient cells.

evidence.snippet: In contrast to other disorders caused by dysregulated mTOR signaling associated with focal or global brain overgrowth, impaired TBCK function results in progressive loss of brain volume.
evidence.explanation: Contrasts the direction of mTOR dysregulation and its structural consequence against the mTORopathy overgrowth disorders.

evidence.snippet: These data showed that loss of TBCK did not inhibit mTORC1 activity in neither NPC nor neurons.
evidence.explanation: Retained as an explicit negative result: the mTORC1 change is absent in the disease-relevant neural cell types.

steps/3.description: Patient fibroblasts and lymphocytes show markedly decreased phosphorylation of ribosomal protein S6, a canonical mTORC1 readout. Unlike most mTOR-pathway neurodevelopmental disorders, which involve mTOR over-activation and brain overgrowth, TBCK deficiency is associated with reduced signaling and progressive loss of brain volume. The finding does not generalize: in human neural progenitors and neurons mTORC1 activity is unchanged, and inhibition across patient lines is inconsistent, so the node is curated as hypothesis-scoped rather than as an established step.

evidence.snippet: which blocks the transition from early to late endosomes and results in the formation of massively enlarged RAB5-positive endosomes. Furthermore, this RAB5 hyperactivation drives the constitutive activation of the PIK3C3/VPS34 complex.
evidence.explanation: Describes the endosomal maturation arrest and its VPS34 consequence.

steps/4.description: Without GAP-mediated GTP hydrolysis, RAB5 remains active, the early-to-late endosome transition is blocked, and massively enlarged RAB5-positive endosomes accumulate. RAB5 hyperactivation also constitutively activates the PIK3C3/VPS34 complex.

evidence.snippet: Alteration in these processes, which are crucial for neurogenesis, neuronal migration, and cytoarchitecture organization, may represent an important causative mechanism of both neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative phenotypes observed in IHPRF3.
evidence.explanation: States the authors' interpretation that these secretory/migration defects underlie the neurodevelopmental phenotype.

evidence.snippet: TBCK knockdown in ReNcells affected NPC differentiation to neurons and astrocytes.
evidence.explanation: Independent human neural progenitor model showing that TBCK loss impairs differentiation.

steps/5.description: In induced neuroprogenitor cells derived from affected individuals, absent TBCK is accompanied by defective early secretory (ER-to-Golgi) vesicle transport, impaired autophagosome biogenesis, altered cell-cycle progression, and severely reduced migratory capacity — processes required for neurogenesis and cortical cytoarchitecture, and therefore a candidate substrate for the neurodevelopmental (as opposed to neurodegenerative) half of the phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Hence, our work reveals that TBCK can mediate endolysosomal trafficking of mRNA, particularly along lysosomes in human axonal compartments. TBCK-deficiency leads to compartment-specific mRNA and lysosomal trafficking defects in neurons, which likely contribute to the preferential susceptibility to neurodegeneration.
evidence.explanation: States both the trafficking defect and the authors' link to selective neuronal vulnerability.

steps/6.description: TBCK localizes preferentially to endolysosomal vesicle surfaces and can co-localize with mRNA in lysosomes. In patient-derived neurons homozygous for the Boricua p.R126X allele, axonal mRNA content is reduced relative to the soma and the lysosomal dynein/dynactin adaptor JIP4 is depleted, producing lysosomal axonal retrograde-trafficking defects. This compartment-specific failure is the leading candidate explanation for why long-projection neurons — and hence motor neurons — are selectively vulnerable.

evidence.snippet: Our comprehensive analysis uncovered significant disruptions in ribosomal and translation-related pathways with widespread alternative splicing defects, and key miRNA changes that validate previously reported molecular findings.
evidence.explanation: The multi-omics result establishing the ribosome, translation and splicing disruption this node asserts.

evidence.snippet: Functional validation through puromycin incorporation assays supported the transcriptomic findings, confirming reduced translation in TBCK−/− cells
evidence.explanation: Direct functional confirmation of the DECREASED direction on the cytoplasmic translation process, independent of the pathway-enrichment result.

steps/7.description: Unbiased transcriptomic and proteomic profiling of patient-derived TBCK-deficient cells shows disruption of ribosomal and translation-related pathways together with widespread alternative-splicing defects and altered miRNA networks, and puromycin-incorporation (SUnSET) assays confirm globally reduced nascent protein synthesis. This is the translational-output arm predicted by TBCK's membership of the FERRY complex - the Five-subunit Endosomal Rab5 and RNA/ribosome intermediarY - whose proposed role is to deliver mRNA to peripheral translation machinery. Measured in fibroblasts rather than neurons, so its relationship to the axonal mRNA-trafficking defect is convergent rather than demonstrated in a single system.

evidence.snippet: TBCK-/- fibroblasts in vitro exhibit increased numbers of LC3+ autophagosomes and increased autophagic flux by immunoblots. Free oligosaccharide profiles in fibroblasts and urine of TBCKE patients differ from control fibroblasts and are ameliorated by treatment with the mTORC1 activator leucine.
evidence.explanation: Documents both the autophagosome excess and the impaired glycoprotein degradation.

evidence.snippet: Our data show that lysosomal proteolytic function is significantly reduced in TBCK -/- fibroblasts.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the degradative endpoint failure.

steps/8.description: Patient fibroblasts accumulate LC3-positive autophagosomes with increased autophagic flux while lysosomal proteolytic capacity is significantly reduced, and degradation of glycosylated proteins is impaired, producing abnormal free oligosaccharide profiles in cells and urine. The combination of excess autophagosome formation with an incompetent degradative endpoint is the convergence point of both curated mechanistic models.

evidence.snippet: Our data show significant accumulation of mitophagosomes, reduced mitochondrial respiratory capacity and mitochondrial DNA content, suggesting impaired mitochondrial quality control. Furthermore, the degree of mitochondrial dysfunction correlates with a neurodegenerative clinical course.
evidence.explanation: Documents the mitochondrial phenotype and its correlation with clinical severity.

evidence.snippet: Further, TBCK knockdown altered mitochondrial dynamics and membrane potential in NPC, neurons and astrocytes. We found partial mitochondrial rescue with the mitochondrial fission inhibitor mdivi-1.
evidence.explanation: Confirms mitochondrial involvement in human neural cells and shows partial pharmacological rescue.

steps/9.description: Mitophagosomes accumulate while mitochondrial respiratory capacity and mtDNA content fall, and the degree of mitochondrial dysfunction tracks with a neurodegenerative clinical course. This is a secondary mitochondriopathy — rescued by acidifying lysosomal nanoparticles — and explains why affected children are frequently investigated for a primary mitochondrial disorder.

evidence.snippet: a widespread and massive accumulation of lipofuscin storage material in neurons of the central nervous system without notable neuronal degeneration, 2) storage deposits in few astrocytes, 3) carbohydrate-rich deposits in brain, spleen and liver and 4) vacuolated lymphocytes
evidence.explanation: The primary neuropathological description of the storage phenotype.

steps/10.description: Post-mortem neuropathology shows widespread, massive accumulation of lipofuscin storage material in CNS neurons, storage deposits in a minority of astrocytes, carbohydrate-rich deposits in brain, spleen and liver, and vacuolated lymphocytes, with more than twenty known lysosomal storage diseases excluded biochemically. Because the predominant deposit is intraneuronal lipofuscin, the authors proposed classifying TBCK deficiency as a new neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis subtype (CLN15); that classification remains a proposal and is not adopted by MONDO.

evidence.snippet: Neuromuscular weakness usually affects the distal muscles first, leading to distal muscle wasting, and then the proximal muscles become involved. Electrophysiologic studies suggest that weakness is secondary to a motor neuronopathy.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews attributes the weakness to a motor neuronopathy.

evidence.snippet: Thus, their electrophysiologic features are most consistent with an anterior horn cell disease or less likely a distal motor neuropathy.
evidence.explanation: Localizes the lesion to the anterior horn cell on the basis of NCS/EMG in a genotyped cohort.

steps/11.description: Nerve conduction studies, EMG and muscle ultrasound in affected children show absent or markedly reduced motor compound muscle action potentials with preserved sensory responses, chronic partial denervation/reinnervation, and fasciculations — a pattern most consistent with anterior horn cell disease. Electrophysiology is essentially normal in infancy and becomes neurogenic later in childhood, so this is an acquired, progressive lesion rather than a developmental one, and it drives the distal-onset muscle wasting and the respiratory failure.

evidence.snippet: brain MRI imaging may show white matter lesions and progressive cortical atrophy over time
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews describes the imaging phenotype and its progression.

evidence.snippet: impaired TBCK function results in progressive loss of brain volume
evidence.explanation: States the progressive nature of the volume loss.

steps/12.description: Brain MRI shows white-matter lesions (ranging from non-specific change to a leukodystrophy-like or periventricular-leukomalacia-like pattern) with progressive cortical atrophy and ex vacuo ventriculomegaly; corpus callosum dysgenesis and cerebellar vermis hypoplasia were described in the original cohort. The loss of brain volume is progressive, distinguishing TBCK deficiency from the overgrowth mTORopathies.

evidence.snippet: Minor non-specific facial dysmorphism was also noted in some individuals, including multiple older children who developed coarse features similar to those of storage disorders.
evidence.explanation: Documents the evolution from minor dysmorphism to coarse facies.

evidence.snippet: coarsening of facial features over time
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews lists the progressive facial coarsening.

steps/13.description: The "characteristic facies" of the disorder name is not a fixed dysmorphic gestalt present at birth but a phenotype that evolves: minor non-specific dysmorphism in infancy that coarsens through childhood, with bitemporal narrowing, macroglossia, high-arched eyebrows, high palate and a tented upper lip, resembling the facies of a lysosomal storage disorder.

evidence.snippet: Respiratory issues are also progressive, with most affected individuals requiring noninvasive nocturnal respiratory support by age five years and about 75% of teenagers requiring a tracheostomy.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the respiratory trajectory.

evidence.snippet: diminished respiratory drive requiring mechanical ventilation
evidence.explanation: The original cohort described diminished central respiratory drive in addition to neuromuscular weakness.

steps/14.description: Progressive hypoventilation from neuromuscular weakness and diminished respiratory drive: most affected individuals require nocturnal non-invasive support by age five and about 75% of teenagers require tracheostomy. Respiratory complications are the usual cause of premature death.

evidence.snippet: A majority of affected individuals do not achieve independent ambulation or spoken language.
evidence.explanation: States the developmental ceiling that defines the phenotype.

evidence.snippet: All affected individuals were found to share a core phenotype of intellectual disability and hypotonia, and many had seizures and showed brain atrophy and white-matter changes on neuroimaging.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the core phenotype across the original multi-family cohort.

steps/15.description: The clinical convergence point: profound global developmental delay and intellectual disability with absent or minimal speech, failure to achieve independent ambulation, epilepsy, and later developmental regression and neurologic decompensation with intercurrent illness.

evidence.snippet: we identify TBCK as the catalytic core of a heterotrimeric complex comprising TBCK, PPP1R21, and FERRY3/C12orf4. This complex functions as a specific GTPase-activating protein (GAP) for RAB5.
evidence.explanation: Identifies TBCK as the catalytic subunit whose loss ablates the GAP activity.

edges/1.description: Absence of TBCK removes the catalytic core of the heterotrimeric RAB5-GAP.

evidence.snippet: decreased phosphorylation of phospho-ribosomal protein S6 was also observed, a finding suggestive of downregulation of mTOR signaling
evidence.explanation: Supports an association between TBCK loss and reduced mTORC1 output; PARTIAL because the authors themselves describe it as suggestive and the mechanism linking the two is unknown.

edges/2.description: Loss of TBCK is associated with reduced basal mTORC1 output in fibroblasts and lymphocytes; the intermediate steps are not established, and the effect is not reproduced in neural cell types.

evidence.snippet: Lack of functional TBCK protein in iNPC is associated with impaired endoplasmic reticulum-to-Golgi vesicle transport and autophagosome biogenesis, as well as altered cell cycle progression and severe impairment in the capacity of migration.
evidence.explanation: Directly links absent TBCK to the early secretory transport defect.

edges/3.description: Patient-derived neuroprogenitor cells lacking functional TBCK show defective early secretory transport.

evidence.snippet: TBCK deficiency or missense mutations of its key residues in the RABGAP-TBC domain lead to constitutive RAB5 hyperactivation, which blocks the transition from early to late endosomes
evidence.explanation: The GAP loss directly produces the RAB5 hyperactivation phenotype.

evidence.snippet: TBCK-deficient neurons have reduced mRNA content in the axonal compartment relative to the soma.
evidence.explanation: Loss of the FERRY subunit produces the compartment-specific mRNA trafficking defect.

evidence.snippet: Our comprehensive analysis uncovered significant disruptions in ribosomal and translation-related pathways with widespread alternative splicing defects, and key miRNA changes that validate previously reported molecular findings.
evidence.explanation: Unbiased multi-omics in patient-derived TBCK-deficient cells identifies the ribosome/translation axis as a consequence of TBCK loss.

edges/6.description: The FERRY complex couples early endosomes to mRNA and ribosomes, so loss of TBCK is expected to degrade translational output; the steps between the lost GAP activity and the measured translation deficit are not established.

evidence.snippet: These defects culminate in a failure of lysosomal enzyme delivery and a secondary collapse of macroautophagic/autophagic flux.
evidence.explanation: The endosomal arrest is stated to cause the lysosomal and autophagic failure.

evidence.snippet: TBCK-/- fibroblasts in vitro exhibit increased numbers of LC3+ autophagosomes and increased autophagic flux by immunoblots.
evidence.explanation: Links the mTORC1-inhibited state to the predicted excess of autophagosomes in patient cells.

evidence.snippet: may represent an important causative mechanism of both neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative phenotypes observed in IHPRF3
evidence.explanation: The authors propose the link; PARTIAL because it is an in vitro-grounded proposal, not a demonstrated in vivo causal chain.

edges/9.description: Impaired neurogenesis and neuronal migration are proposed to contribute to the structural brain phenotype, but the intermediate steps in vivo are not established.

evidence.snippet: which likely contribute to the preferential susceptibility to neurodegeneration
evidence.explanation: The authors state the link as likely rather than demonstrated, so the edge is recorded as partially supported.

edges/10.description: Proposed link between the axonal trafficking defect and the selective degeneration of long-projection motor neurons; the intervening steps are not established.

evidence.snippet: neurons in particular utilize the machinery for intracellular organelle trafficking for mRNAs to “hitchhike” along organelles to be delivered for local protein translation
evidence.explanation: Establishes the premise the edge depends on - that organelle trafficking is how neurons deliver mRNA to local translation machinery. PARTIAL and OTHER because this is a background statement of the field's model within the paper, not a result measured in TBCK-deficient cells.

evidence.snippet: These results support the idea that TBCK deficiency can disrupt core components of the translational machinery across different cell types.
evidence.explanation: Directly addresses the caveat in this edge's description: the same translational-machinery disruption is seen beyond fibroblasts, which is what makes the fibroblast-measured deficit relevant to a neuronal node. PARTIAL because cross-cell-type consistency is not the same as demonstrating the axonal-trafficking route.

edges/11.description: Failure to deliver mRNA to the periphery is the expected route to a translational deficit. Recorded as indirect and unquantified because the translation measurements were made in patient fibroblasts, which have no axonal compartment - the convergence of the two observations is inferred, not demonstrated in one cell type.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, acidifying lysosomal nanoparticles rescue the mitochondrial respiratory defects in fibroblasts, suggesting impaired mitochondrial quality control secondary to lysosomal dysfunction.
evidence.explanation: Rescue by lysosomal acidification places the mitochondrial defect downstream of the lysosomal one.

evidence.snippet: Our results and previous reports suggest an autophagosomal-lysosomal dysfunction caused by enhanced mTORC1-mediated autophagosome formation and reduced Rab-mediated autophagosome-lysosome fusion, thus disclosing potential novel targets for therapeutic approaches in TBCK-DD.
evidence.explanation: The neuropathology authors attribute the storage material to autophagosomal-lysosomal dysfunction.

evidence.snippet: the degree of mitochondrial dysfunction correlates with a neurodegenerative clinical course
evidence.explanation: A correlation between the cellular mitochondrial defect and clinical neurodegeneration; PARTIAL because correlation in fibroblasts is not a demonstrated causal link to brain atrophy.

edges/14.description: Mitochondrial dysfunction severity tracks with the neurodegenerative course, but the relationship established to date is correlative.

evidence.snippet: including multiple older children who developed coarse features similar to those of storage disorders
evidence.explanation: Notes the storage-disorder-like facial evolution; PARTIAL because the resemblance is descriptive, not a demonstrated causal link.

edges/15.description: The progressive coarse facies and macroglossia phenotypically resemble a lysosomal storage disorder; the causal chain from tissue storage to the facial gestalt is inferred rather than demonstrated.

evidence.snippet: Nocturnal ventilatory support and/or tracheostomy may be required for those who have apnea and/or progressive neuromuscular weakness.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews links the ventilatory requirement to the progressive neuromuscular weakness.

evidence.snippet: many had seizures and showed brain atrophy and white-matter changes on neuroimaging
evidence.explanation: Co-occurrence of the structural brain phenotype with the clinical syndrome in the same cohort; PARTIAL because the imaging-to-impairment link is associative.

evidence.snippet: Biallelic inactivating mutations in TBCK (TBC1-domain-containing kinase) were independently identified by whole-exome sequencing as the cause of this condition in four unrelated families.
evidence.explanation: Establishes TBCK as the causal gene.

evidence.snippet: The diagnosis of TBCK-NDD is established in a proband with suggestive findings and biallelic pathogenic variants in TBCK identified by molecular genetic testing.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews states the molecular diagnostic criterion.

evidence.snippet: Gastrostomy tube placement may be required for ongoing feeding issues and/or dysphagia.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews management recommendation.

treatments/0.description: Enteral feeding via gastrostomy for ongoing feeding difficulty and dysphagia, protecting airway safety and nutrition.

evidence.snippet: Nocturnal ventilatory support and/or tracheostomy may be required for those who have apnea and/or progressive neuromuscular weakness.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews management recommendation.

evidence.snippet: Five individuals were diagnosed with hypoventilation, requiring respiratory support, highlighting the need for early respiratory surveillance.
evidence.explanation: Supports early respiratory surveillance and support.

treatments/1.description: Ventilatory support for apnea, nocturnal hypoventilation and progressive neuromuscular respiratory failure; most affected individuals need nocturnal support by age five and about 75% of teenagers proceed to tracheostomy. Sleep studies are indicated based on clinical concern.

evidence.snippet: Nocturnal ventilatory support and/or tracheostomy may be required for those who have apnea and/or progressive neuromuscular weakness.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews ties the intervention directly to the respiratory-insufficiency node it addresses.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Supportive, not disease-modifying: ventilation substitutes for the failing respiratory pump without altering the underlying motor neuronopathy.

evidence.snippet: Standard treatment for developmental delay / intellectual disability / neurobehavioral issues, epilepsy, neuromuscular weakness, spasticity/ contractures, growth deficiency, bowel dysfunction, pancreatitis, osteopenia / frequent fractures, eye/vision issues, left ventricular hypertrophy, recurrent urinary tract infections, nephrolithiasis, and neurogenic bladder.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews specifies standard symptomatic management, including for epilepsy.

treatments/2.description: Standard treatment for epilepsy; seizures may be medication-refractory, and monitoring is recommended as clinically indicated.

evidence.snippet: assess for developmental progress and educational needs; assess for neurobehavioral concerns; and assess for progressive contractures and bony fractures
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews surveillance guidance underpinning the rehabilitation and developmental-support recommendation.

treatments/3.description: Physical, occupational and speech therapy plus orthopedic management for contractures and neuromuscular scoliosis; developmental and educational support. No disease-modifying therapy exists.

evidence.snippet: Some affected individuals have been reported to have adverse effects to bisphosphonate infusions for management of osteoporosis. The frequency and mechanism of this observation in the TBCK-NDD population remain unclear, so close monitoring is advised if bisphosphonates are clinically indicated.
evidence.explanation: The GeneReviews "Agents/circumstances to avoid" caution; PARTIAL because the source records a safety signal of unclear frequency rather than an established contraindication or an efficacy claim.

treatments/4.description: Bisphosphonates may be clinically indicated for osteoporosis, but adverse reactions to bisphosphonate infusions have been reported in affected individuals. The frequency and mechanism are unclear, so close monitoring is advised. This is the disorder's documented "agents to avoid" caveat.

evidence.snippet: Free oligosaccharide profiles in fibroblasts and urine of TBCKE patients differ from control fibroblasts and are ameliorated by treatment with the mTORC1 activator leucine.
evidence.explanation: In vitro rescue of a disease biomarker; PARTIAL because no clinical efficacy data exist in affected individuals.

treatments/5.description: Leucine activates mTORC1 and, in patient fibroblasts, restores phospho-S6 signaling and normalizes the abnormal free oligosaccharide profile. It has been proposed as a directed therapy but has not been tested in a clinical trial, and its rationale rests on the mTORC1 model, which is not reproduced in neural cell types.

evidence.snippet: we demonstrated that activation of the mTOR pathway in response to L-leucine supplementation was retained, suggesting a possible avenue for directed therapies for this condition.
evidence.explanation: Shows the pathway remains leucine-responsive, which is the entire basis of this candidate therapy.

treatments/5/targets/0.description: Exogenous leucine activates the retained mTORC1 signaling machinery in TBCK-deficient cells.

evidence.snippet: It also supports the benefit of lysosomal acidification strategies for disorders of impaired lysosomal degradation affecting mitochondrial quality control.
evidence.explanation: Authors propose the strategy on in vitro evidence; PARTIAL because no in vivo or clinical data exist.

treatments/6.description: Acidifying lysosomal nanoparticles rescue the mitochondrial respiratory defect in TBCK-deficient patient fibroblasts, supporting lysosomal acidification as a candidate therapeutic strategy. Preclinical only.

evidence.snippet: acidifying lysosomal nanoparticles rescue the mitochondrial respiratory defects in fibroblasts
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates the rescue in patient-derived cells.

evidence.snippet: TBCK deficiency or missense mutations of its key residues in the RABGAP-TBC domain lead to constitutive RAB5 hyperactivation, which blocks the transition from early to late endosomes and results in the formation of massively enlarged RAB5-positive endosomes.
evidence.explanation: States the proposed primary molecular lesion of this model.

evidence.snippet: TBCK-deficient neurons show reduced levels of the lysosomal dynein/dynactin adapter protein JIP4, which functionally leads to TBCK-deficient neurons exhibiting striking lysosomal axonal retrograde trafficking defects.
evidence.explanation: Patient-derived neurons show the endolysosomal trafficking phenotype this model predicts.

hypotheses/0.description: TBCK is the catalytic core of a TBCK-PPP1R21-FERRY3 heterotrimer that acts as a RAB5 GTPase-activating protein and is a subunit of the wider FERRY complex that shuttles mRNA on early endosomes for local translation. Under this model the primary lesion is constitutive RAB5 hyperactivation with arrest of the early-to-late endosome transition, failure of lysosomal enzyme delivery, and compartment-specific mRNA/lysosome trafficking failure in axons; autophagic, lysosomal-storage and mitochondrial abnormalities and any mTORC1 change are downstream consequences.

evidence.snippet: TBCK was absent in cells from affected individuals, and decreased phosphorylation of phospho-ribosomal protein S6 was also observed, a finding suggestive of downregulation of mTOR signaling.
evidence.explanation: The original observation on which the mTORC1 model rests.

evidence.snippet: These data showed that loss of TBCK did not inhibit mTORC1 activity in neither NPC nor neurons. Additionally, analysis of eight patient-derived cells and TBCK knock down HeLa cells showed that mTORC1 inhibition is inconsistent across different patients and cell types.
evidence.explanation: A human neural model finds no mTORC1 inhibition in the disease-relevant cell types, directly challenging this model.

hypotheses/1.description: The original model: loss of TBCK Rab-GAP function downregulates mTORC1 signaling, and the resulting de-repression of autophagy drives autophagic-lysosomal dysfunction and neurodegeneration. It is supported by reduced phospho-S6 in patient fibroblasts and lymphocytes and by rescue of fibroblast oligosaccharide profiles with the mTORC1 activator leucine, but is contradicted in neural cell types, where mTORC1 activity is unchanged and where the inhibition seen across patient lines is inconsistent. Retained as an alternative because it is the basis of the only proposed disease-directed therapy (leucine supplementation).

evidence.snippet: Whether reduced mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling is secondary to impaired TBCK function over other secretory transport regulators still needs further investigation.
evidence.explanation: The authors state the open question in these terms.

open_questions/0.rationale: The mTORC1 model is the basis of the only proposed disease-directed therapy (leucine supplementation), so whether it is causal matters clinically, not just taxonomically. Reduced phospho-S6 is reproducible in patient fibroblasts and lymphocytes, but a human neural model found no mTORC1 inhibition in neuroprogenitors or neurons and found the effect inconsistent across eight patient-derived lines. The iNPC authors likewise leave open whether reduced mTOR signaling is secondary to impaired regulation of other secretory transport regulators.

evidence.snippet: Due to the clear predominance of intraneuronal lipofuscin storage material and the characteristic clinical presentation we propose to classify this disease as a new subtype of neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (CLN15).
evidence.explanation: States the proposal; the question mark in the paper's own title signals it is unsettled.

evidence.snippet: These findings redefine TBCK syndrome as a primary disorder of endosomal dynamics
evidence.explanation: The competing framing that would place the storage downstream of a trafficking defect rather than defining the disease class.

open_questions/1.rationale: Neuropathology shows predominant intraneuronal lipofuscin, prompting a CLN15 proposal. But the storage is heterogeneous rather than a single substrate, there is no deficient lysosomal hydrolase, and the emerging mechanism is a RAB5-GAP/trafficking defect that impairs lysosomal enzyme delivery rather than enzyme function. MONDO does not classify IHPRF3 under the neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses, and no lysosomal_storage classification is asserted in this entry pending resolution.

open_questions/2.rationale: The numbered IHPRF series shares a clinical presentation but not a mechanism. NALCN and UNC80 encode components of one sodium-leak channelosome, whereas TBCK acts on an unrelated endolysosomal/FERRY axis, and IHPRF3 alone carries the progressive neurodegenerative course with lysosomal storage. This entry is therefore curated standalone. Tracked in dismech issue #8451, which proposes a NALCN/UNC80 channelosome entry plus this separate TBCK entry.

evidence.snippet: MSMD confers a selective susceptibility to infections with weakly virulent mycobacteria, including the M. bovis Bacille Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccines
evidence.explanation: Establishes BCG vaccine exposure as a defining trigger of clinical disease in this disease family.

evidence.snippet: We report a patient with mycobacterial disease due to inherited deficiency of the transcription factor T-bet.
evidence.explanation: Establishes inherited T-bet deficiency as the initiating molecular lesion.

evidence.snippet: T box domain of T box proteins might bind the target sequence as a dimer, interacting with both the major and the minor grooves of the DNA
evidence.explanation: Supports the molecular-function annotation of T-bet as a sequence-specific DNA-binding transcription factor.

steps/2.description: The initiating lesion is biallelic loss of function of TBX21, abolishing functional T-bet. T-bet is a sequence-specific DNA-binding transcription factor of the T-box family and is the master regulator of the type 1 immune program; its loss removes the transcriptional instruction that specifies the IFN-gamma-producing lineages rather than any component of the IL-12/IFN-gamma signalling circuit itself.

evidence.snippet: Unlike wild-type (WT) T-bet, the mutant form of T-bet from this patient did not inhibit the production of Th2 cytokines, including IL-4, IL-5, IL-9, and IL-13, when overexpressed in T helper 2 (Th2) cells.
evidence.explanation: Establishes loss of the Th2-repressive function of T-bet as a distinct molecular consequence of the same variant.

steps/3.description: T-bet is not only the activator of the type 1 program; it is also a repressor of the type 2 one. The patient's mutant T-bet, unlike the wild-type protein, fails to inhibit production of the Th2 cytokines IL-4, IL-5, IL-9 and IL-13 when overexpressed in Th2 cells. A single transcription-factor lesion therefore produces two opposite-signed defects at once, and this repressive arm is what gives IMD88 an allergic phenotype on top of its infectious one.

evidence.snippet: 89% (2208) of these 2478 differentially regulated loci remained unaltered in CpG/αIg/IFN-γ-stimulated T-bet-deficient B cells
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the accessibility defect in the patient's B cells: the great majority of loci that normally change on stimulation do not.

steps/4.description: The molecular step between the transcription-factor lesion and the B cell outcome. T-bet governs the CD11c-high CD21-low differentiation program by controlling chromatin accessibility at a defined set of lineage-defining genes — FAS, IL21R, SEC61B, DUSP4, DAPP1, SOX5, CD79B and CXCR4. Without T-bet those loci do not open: 89% of the 2478 loci differentially regulated in stimulated healthy B cells remained unaltered in the patient's. This is what makes the requirement structural rather than a matter of transcriptional tuning, and it is the reason the subset fails to form at all rather than forming at reduced numbers.

evidence.snippet: The patient has extremely low counts of circulating Mycobacterium-reactive natural killer (NK), invariant NKT (iNKT), mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT), and Vδ2+ γδ T lymphocytes, and of Mycobacterium-non reactive classic TH1 lymphocytes
evidence.explanation: Direct enumeration of the depleted lineages in the patient.

evidence.snippet: Deficiency of T-bet leads to significantly reduced NK cell numbers
evidence.explanation: Mouse genetic data independently support T-bet as a requirement for the NK compartment, corroborating the human developmental defect.

steps/5.description: Without T-bet, the innate (NK) and innate-like adaptive (iNKT, MAIT, Vdelta2+ gamma-delta T) lymphocyte lineages fail to develop, and circulating counts of the Mycobacterium-reactive members of these populations are extremely low. Classic TH1 lymphocytes, which are Mycobacterium-non-reactive, are also severely depleted. This is a developmental rather than a signalling defect, which is what distinguishes IMD88 from the receptor and JAK-STAT etiologies of MSMD.

evidence.snippet: Other lymphocyte subsets develop normally but produce low levels of IFN-γ, with the exception of CD8+ αβ T and non-classic CD4+ αβ TH1∗ lymphocytes, which produce IFN-γ normally in response to mycobacterial antigens.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that this compartment is functionally intact, which is what makes its failure to compensate a substantive finding rather than a second deficit.

steps/6.description: CD8+ alpha-beta T and non-classic CD4+ alpha-beta TH1* lymphocytes are spared by the T-bet lesion and produce IFN-gamma normally in response to mycobacterial antigens. They nonetheless fail to compensate for the missing innate and innate-like output. This negative result is the disease's central mechanistic finding: it establishes that the innate and innate-like IFN-gamma compartments are non-redundant for anti-mycobacterial immunity in humans, and it is why the residual adaptive response does not rescue the phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Herpesvirus saimiri-immortalized T cells from the patient produced abnormally large amounts of Th2 cytokines
evidence.explanation: Documents the Th2 cytokine overproduction in patient-derived cells.

evidence.snippet: the patient had markedly high plasma IL-5 and IL-13 concentrations
evidence.explanation: Gives the systemic in vivo correlate of the cellular overproduction. Quoted separately from the in vitro finding in the same sentence because the two are different kinds of evidence.

evidence.snippet: T-bet deficiency thus underlies the excessive production of Th2 cytokines, particularly IL-5 and IL-13, by CD4+ αβ T cells, causing blood eosinophilia and UAI.
evidence.explanation: States the causal chain from T-bet loss through CD4+ Th2 cytokine excess to the two clinical consequences recorded as downstream phenotypes.

steps/7.description: The patient's CD4+ alpha-beta T lymphocytes produce most of the Th2 cytokines on chronic stimulation, and do so regardless of antigen specificity — the defect is a loss of restraint on the program rather than an antigen-directed response. Note the compartment: this is the same purely adaptive CD4+ alpha-beta population that is spared by, and cannot compensate for, the type 1 arm of the disease. One compartment thus carries both the disease's failure to help and its excess.

evidence.snippet: Thus, human T-bet is largely redundant for long-lived protective humoral immunity but is essential for the development of a distinct subset of human CD11chiCD21lo B cells.
evidence.explanation: States both halves of this node: humoral immunity is broadly spared, and one specific B cell subset is T-bet-dependent.

evidence.snippet: Nevertheless, the patient exhibited skewed class switching to IgG1, IgG4, and IgE, along with reduced IgG2, both in vivo and in vitro.
evidence.explanation: Documents the class-switch skewing that produces the immunoglobulin phenotypes recorded downstream of this node.

steps/8.description: A third consequence of the same lesion, in a third compartment. T-bet is dispensable for the bulk of humoral immunity in humans — somatic hypermutation, affinity maturation, memory and plasmablast formation, and vaccine-specific antibody titres are all intact — but it is required for one specific B cell subset (CD11c-high CD21-low) and it biases immunoglobulin class switching. The patient's isotype profile is skewed toward IgG1, IgG4 and IgE and away from IgG2. The IgE limb is not incidental: it runs in the same type-2 direction as the Th2 excess, which is consistent with a common loss of T-bet restraint on type 2 responses.

evidence.snippet: with the residual populations of these cells also producing abnormally small amounts of IFN-γ
evidence.explanation: Establishes the second component of the deficit: the surviving cells are themselves hypofunctional for IFN-gamma.

steps/9.description: The net result is insufficient IFN-gamma at the site of mycobacterial challenge. The deficit is quantitative and has two components: the cells that would normally supply the cytokine are largely absent, and the residual members of those populations each secrete abnormally small amounts. Human IFN-gamma level behaves as a quantitative trait determining the outcome of mycobacterial infection, so a partial deficit is sufficient to produce disease.

evidence.snippet: almost all genetic etiologies of MSMD alter the interferon-gamma (IFN-γ)- mediated immunity by impairing or abolishing IFN-γ production or the response to this cytokine
evidence.explanation: Establishes IFN-gamma-mediated immunity as the common convergence point of MSMD, of which macrophage activation is the effector arm.

steps/10.description: IFN-gamma is the signal that licenses macrophages to kill ingested mycobacteria. With the cytokine in short supply, the macrophage antimicrobial program is not engaged. This is the step at which every MSMD etiology converges, whether the upstream lesion impairs IFN-gamma production - documented for TBX21 - or the response to it, or, as in some etiologies, both; whether TBX21 deficiency also blunts the response to IFN-gamma has not been tested.

evidence.snippet: MSMD confers a selective susceptibility to infections with weakly virulent mycobacteria, including the M. bovis Bacille Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccines and various environmental mycobacteria in patients, primarily children, without classical immune defects.
evidence.explanation: Describes the organism-level outcome and its selectivity, which is the content of this node.

steps/11.description: Mycobacteria that a competent host clears without difficulty — the M. bovis BCG vaccine strain and environmental non-tuberculous species — replicate unchecked and disseminate. The susceptibility is selective: these patients are not broadly vulnerable to all pathogens, which is the clinical signature that distinguishes MSMD from combined immunodeficiency.

evidence.snippet: MSMD confers a selective susceptibility to infections with weakly virulent mycobacteria, including the M. bovis Bacille Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccines
evidence.explanation: Establishes BCG disease as a defining clinical manifestation of MSMD, the syndrome this TBX21 etiology produces.

steps/12.description: Disseminated disease caused by the M. bovis BCG vaccine strain following routine vaccination. In countries with universal BCG programmes this is typically the presenting event of MSMD, since it is the first mycobacterial challenge an infant meets.

evidence.snippet: MSMD confers a selective susceptibility to infections with weakly virulent mycobacteria, including the M. bovis Bacille Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccines and various environmental mycobacteria in patients, primarily children, without classical immune defects.
evidence.explanation: Establishes susceptibility to environmental mycobacteria as a defining feature of MSMD, the syndrome this TBX21 etiology produces.

evidence.snippet: he has been in remission and free of mycobacterial infection for several years
evidence.explanation: Does not bear on whether the susceptibility exists — it reports the outcome of the one treated episode. Recorded here so a reader does not infer a recurrent or relapsing course from the class-level susceptibility above; the sentence is cited as evidence of course under `progression`, where that is the claim being made.

steps/13.description: Susceptibility to weakly virulent environmental non-tuberculous mycobacteria. In countries that do not vaccinate with BCG these organisms, rather than the vaccine strain, are the usual precipitant of MSMD. Recorded as the class-level susceptibility of the syndrome: the index patient was ascertained through BCG disease, was cured, and has remained free of mycobacterial infection for several years, so he is not an example of a recurrent or NTM course. HP:0011274 Recurrent mycobacterial infections is deliberately not bound anywhere in this entry for that reason.

evidence.snippet: These patients may also present severe forms of tuberculosis, and about half of them might develop non-typhoidal salmonellosis.
evidence.explanation: Extends the MSMD infectious spectrum to severe tuberculosis. Quoted for the tuberculosis clause; the salmonellosis clause is curated as its own phenotype.

steps/14.description: Susceptibility to severe forms of tuberculosis, over and above the susceptibility to weakly virulent mycobacteria. Recorded as the MSMD-wide spectrum, not as an observed event in the index patient. The HPO term's own definition names MSMD as one of the inborn errors in which disseminated tuberculosis is characteristic.

evidence.snippet: These patients may also present severe forms of tuberculosis, and about half of them might develop non-typhoidal salmonellosis.
evidence.explanation: Cohort-level frequency of non-typhoidal salmonellosis in MSMD; applied here as syndromic context, not as a TBX21-specific finding.

steps/15.description: About half of MSMD patients develop non-typhoidal salmonellosis, reflecting the same dependence on IFN-gamma-activated macrophages for control of intracellular bacteria. As with lymphadenopathy, this is the MSMD-wide figure and is recorded as the expected syndromic spectrum; it is not reported in the TBX21-deficient patient, whose only documented infection was the BCG episode.

evidence.snippet: The patient has extremely low counts of circulating Mycobacterium-reactive natural killer (NK), invariant NKT (iNKT), mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT), and Vδ2+ γδ T lymphocytes
evidence.explanation: Reports the reduced NK count directly in the affected patient.

steps/16.description: Circulating Mycobacterium-reactive NK lymphocytes are present at extremely low counts, reflecting the failure of the T-bet-dependent NK developmental program.

evidence.snippet: The patient has extremely low counts of circulating Mycobacterium-reactive natural killer (NK), invariant NKT (iNKT), mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT), and Vδ2+ γδ T lymphocytes
evidence.explanation: Reports the reduced MAIT count directly in the affected patient.

steps/17.description: MAIT lymphocytes are among the innate-like adaptive lineages that fail to develop without T-bet, and circulating Mycobacterium-reactive MAIT counts are extremely low.

evidence.snippet: The patient has extremely low counts of circulating Mycobacterium-reactive natural killer (NK), invariant NKT (iNKT), mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT), and Vδ2+ γδ T lymphocytes
evidence.explanation: Reports the reduced Vdelta2+ gamma-delta T cell count directly in the affected patient.

steps/18.description: Vdelta2+ gamma-delta T lymphocytes, the innate-like gamma-delta subset that responds to mycobacterial phosphoantigens, are present at extremely low counts.

evidence.snippet: and of Mycobacterium-non reactive classic TH1 lymphocytes, with the residual populations of these cells also producing abnormally small amounts of IFN-γ
evidence.explanation: Reports depletion of classic TH1 lymphocytes alongside the innate-like lineages.

steps/19.description: Classic TH1 lymphocytes are severely depleted, consistent with T-bet's canonical role as the TH1 lineage-specifying transcription factor. Note that these cells are Mycobacterium-non-reactive in this patient, so their loss is a marker of the transcriptional lesion rather than the direct cause of the mycobacterial susceptibility.

evidence.snippet: Lymphadenopathy was the most common clinical manifestation of MSMD, reported in 378 (45.5%) cases and multifocal in 35.1%.
evidence.explanation: Cohort-level frequency of lymphadenopathy in MSMD; applied here as the syndromic context for this etiology, not as a TBX21-specific rate.

steps/20.description: Lymphadenopathy, frequently multifocal, is the single most common clinical manifestation across the MSMD patient population. The frequency figure below is for MSMD as a whole rather than for the TBX21 etiology specifically, which has too few reported patients to support an etiology-specific estimate; it is recorded here as the expected syndromic presentation.

evidence.snippet: T-bet deficiency thus underlies the excessive production of Th2 cytokines, particularly IL-5 and IL-13, by CD4+ αβ T cells, causing blood eosinophilia and UAI.
evidence.explanation: Attributes the patient's blood eosinophilia to the Th2 cytokine excess caused by T-bet deficiency.

steps/21.description: Blood eosinophilia in the reported patient, driven by the IL-5 excess that follows loss of T-bet repression of the Th2 program. This is a consequence of the same variant as the mycobacterial susceptibility but reaches the clinic by an entirely separate route, so it is not a marker of infection severity.

evidence.snippet: Here, we explore the persistent upper airway inflammation (UAI) and blood eosinophilia of this patient.
evidence.explanation: Documents persistent upper airway inflammation as a clinical feature of the reported T-bet-deficient patient.

steps/22.description: Persistent upper airway inflammation in the reported patient, described alongside the blood eosinophilia as the allergic arm of the disease and attributed to the same Th2 cytokine excess.

evidence.snippet: Plasma IgA and IgM levels in P were normal, while IgE was elevated
evidence.explanation: Reports the elevated plasma IgE alongside normal IgA and IgM, which localises the defect to class switching rather than to antibody production generally.

steps/23.description: Elevated plasma IgE, part of the class-switch skew toward IgG1, IgG4 and IgE that follows loss of T-bet. It sits on the same type-2 axis as the Th2 cytokine excess and the eosinophilia.

evidence.snippet: Plasma total IgG levels were also higher in P, predominantly due to increased IgG1, and a modest increase in IgG4 (Fig. 1D). By contrast, IgG2 was reduced
evidence.explanation: Reports the full immunoglobulin subclass profile in the patient: total IgG and IgG1 up, IgG4 modestly up, IgG2 down.

steps/24.description: Reduced plasma IgG2, the opposite limb of the same class-switch skew, present both in vivo and in vitro and mirrored by fewer IgG2+ memory B cells.

evidence.snippet: Fever was described in 251 (30.2%) patients
evidence.explanation: Cohort-level frequency of fever in MSMD; applied here as syndromic context, not as a TBX21-specific rate.

steps/25.description: Fever is the second most common presenting manifestation across the MSMD patient population, after lymphadenopathy. As with lymphadenopathy, the frequency below is for MSMD as a whole rather than for the TBX21 etiology, and is recorded as the expected syndromic presentation.

evidence.snippet: Organomegaly was reported in 206 patients (24.8%)
evidence.explanation: Cohort-level frequency of organomegaly in MSMD; applied here as syndromic context, not as a TBX21-specific rate.

steps/26.description: Organomegaly is the third most common manifestation in the MSMD cohort, split across splenomegaly, hepatomegaly and hepatosplenomegaly. Bound to the combined term because the entry records the organomegaly finding as a whole rather than one organ; the per-organ breakdown is in the cited source. MSMD-wide figure, not TBX21-specific.

evidence.snippet: In patients with MSMD, 39% reported left axillary lymphadenopathy, 13% had proven tuberculosis, 13% reported salmonellosis, 13% reported bilateral necrotic cervical lymphadenopathy with fistula, and 13% reported asthma.
evidence.explanation: Gives an MSMD-population frequency for asthma, which is what allows it to be curated without resting on the single patient's airway phenotype.

steps/27.description: Asthma is reported in 13% of a Moroccan MSMD cohort. It is curated here as MSMD-wide syndromic context, on the same footing as lymphadenopathy and fever, which sidesteps the question the single index patient cannot settle — his type-2 disease is described as upper airway inflammation, and lower-airway involvement is neither reported nor excluded. This phenotype is the HPO-bound distal terminus of the Th2 de-repression branch, which otherwise ends in an unbound free-text phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Human T-bet deficiency thus underlies mycobacterial disease by preventing the development of innate (NK) and innate-like adaptive lymphocytes (iNKT, MAIT, and Vδ2+ γδ T cells)
evidence.explanation: States the causal step directly: T-bet deficiency prevents the development of these lineages.

edges/1.description: Loss of the T-bet transcriptional program removes the lineage-specification signal for the NK, iNKT, MAIT and Vdelta2+ gamma-delta T compartments.

evidence.snippet: Unlike wild-type (WT) T-bet, the mutant form of T-bet from this patient did not inhibit the production of Th2 cytokines, including IL-4, IL-5, IL-9, and IL-13, when overexpressed in T helper 2 (Th2) cells.
evidence.explanation: Direct comparison of wild-type and patient-mutant T-bet establishes that the variant specifically abolishes Th2 repression, which is this causal edge.
