Its function is unknown and its expression is brain- and heart-predominant rather than skeletal, so it is recorded as a cooperating rather than a primary locus — the defining study proposes that combined SULF1 and SLCO5A1 haploinsufficiency, or a position effect on a neighbouring gene, may be what is required.

open_questions/0.rationale: Every reported patient has both genes deleted, so the two-gene hypothesis has never been tested against the one-gene alternative in humans. The question decides whether an isolated SULF1 loss-of-function variant found incidentally should be reported as causal for this syndrome — a question a diagnostic laboratory will eventually face — and it is answerable either by a patient with a smaller deletion or by a single-gene mouse model.

evidence.snippet: We demonstrate that the altered sequence did not affect IND1 mRNA stability, yet it led to a decrease in Ind1 protein level.
evidence.explanation: Locates the effect of the branch-site allele at the protein rather than the transcript level, which is the specific molecular claim this node makes.

evidence.snippet: The instability of mutant Ind1 resulted in a strong decrease in complex I activity and caused slow growth, resembling the phenotype of the deletion strain of IND1.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the instability is sufficient to reproduce a null-like complex I phenotype, which is what makes a 1.2%-frequency allele credible as pathogenic.

evidence.snippet: Complex I function in the yeast model was impacted by p.L104P but not p.V182A.
evidence.explanation: Shows the missense alleles are not functionally equivalent, which bears on variant interpretation in this gene.

steps/1.description: Biallelic NUBPL variants reduce functional NUBPL protein. The recurrent allele is the branch-site variant c.815-27T>C, present in all reported families and in roughly 1.2% of European haplotypes, which produces a frameshifted, altered C-terminus. Modelling that altered C-terminus in the yeast homologue Ind1 showed the mechanism is protein instability rather than transcript loss: mRNA was unaffected while protein level fell. Not every missense allele is equally damaging - p.Leu104Pro impaired complex I function in the yeast model while p.Val182Ala did not.

evidence.snippet: Analysis of the effect of mutated NUBPL on the assembly of the peripheral arm of complex I indicated that NUBPL is involved in assembly of iron-sulfur clusters early in the complex I assembly pathway.
evidence.explanation: Places the lesion at iron-sulfur cluster insertion early in assembly, in patient fibroblasts, which is precisely what this node asserts.

steps/2.description: NUBPL is an iron-sulfur cluster assembly factor for complex I. Analysis of how mutant NUBPL affects assembly of the peripheral arm placed its role early in the complex I assembly pathway, at the stage where iron-sulfur clusters are inserted. The peripheral arm is the electron-transferring limb of the complex, so a cluster-insertion failure there prevents the holoenzyme being completed rather than degrading an assembled enzyme's performance.

evidence.snippet: A strongly decreased amount of NUBPL protein and fully assembled complex I was found in patients' fibroblasts.
evidence.explanation: Measures both the reduced assembly factor and the reduced assembled holoenzyme in the same patient cells.

evidence.snippet: including cDNA complementation to show that mutations in NUBPL and FOXRED1 can cause complex I deficiency
evidence.explanation: The rescue experiment that establishes NUBPL mutations as causal for complex I deficiency rather than merely co-occurring with it.

steps/3.description: Patient fibroblasts show a strongly decreased amount of both NUBPL protein and fully assembled complex I. cDNA complementation restoring NUBPL rescues the defect, which is what established causality in the original cohort rather than leaving the association correlative.

evidence.snippet: Mitochondrial function studies on patient fibroblasts showed significantly reduced spare respiratory capacity.
evidence.explanation: The functional readout of the complex I defect in patient cells, and the specific bioenergetic parameter affected.

evidence.snippet: The 4 tested patients had a respiratory chain complex І deficiency.
evidence.explanation: Confirms biochemical complex I deficiency in the imaging-selected cohort. Quoted verbatim, including the Cyrillic capital I the source uses in place of a Latin I in "complex І".

steps/4.description: Complex I is the entry point of the respiratory chain, transferring electrons from NADH to ubiquinone while pumping protons. With the holoenzyme depleted, oxidative phosphorylation capacity falls. In patient fibroblasts the measurable consequence is significantly reduced spare respiratory capacity - the reserve a cell can call on above baseline demand - which is why tissues with high and fluctuating energy demand are affected first.

evidence.snippet: We identified 6 patients from 5 unrelated families with a similar MRI pattern showing predominant abnormalities of the cerebellar cortex, deep cerebral white matter, and corpus callosum.
evidence.explanation: Defines the anatomical distribution this node represents, across six patients from five unrelated families.

steps/5.description: The imaging signature is predominant abnormality of the cerebellar cortex, deep cerebral white matter and corpus callosum, with cerebellar atrophy. Why this particular distribution follows from a generalised complex I assembly defect is not established, so the edge from the bioenergetic lesion is recorded as indirect with unknown intermediates rather than as a direct consequence.

evidence.snippet: NUBPL mutations cause early onset, autosomal recessive generalized dystonia with cerebellar ataxia, pyramidal signs, preserved cognition and a distinct magnetic resonance imaging appearance with BSN and cerebellar atrophy.
evidence.explanation: States the alternative presentation, its imaging correlate, and the preserved cognition that distinguishes it.

steps/6.description: A separate imaging and clinical presentation: generalized dystonia with pyramidal and cerebellar involvement, bilateral striatal necrosis and cerebellar atrophy, with preserved cognition. Described in a single UK kindred. Whether this is a distinct end of one spectrum or a separate phenotype is unresolved - see the discussion attached to this node.

evidence.snippet: Clinical features include onset of neurological symptoms at 3-18 months, global developmental delay, cerebellar dysfunction (including ataxia, dysarthria, nystagmus and tremor) and spasticity.
evidence.explanation: The clinical feature summary across five newly reported patients, including onset window.

steps/7.description: Onset of neurological symptoms between 3 and 18 months, with global developmental delay.

evidence.snippet: Gaits of Patients 1A and 2 were described as  wide-based and ataxic
evidence.explanation: The gait description that supports binding gait ataxia specifically rather than ataxia in general. Quoted with the source's own double space after "as".

evidence.snippet: cerebellar dysfunction (including ataxia, dysarthria, nystagmus and tremor) and spasticity
evidence.explanation: Places the ataxia inside the wider cerebellar syndrome. On its own this sentence says only "ataxia", which is why the gait-specific quote above carries the HP:0002066 binding.

steps/8.description: Cerebellar dysfunction is the clinical core, presenting as ataxia together with dysarthria, nystagmus and tremor.

evidence.snippet: cerebellar dysfunction (including ataxia, dysarthria, nystagmus and tremor)
evidence.explanation: Lists dysarthria among the cerebellar features.

steps/9.description: Part of the cerebellar syndrome.

evidence.snippet: cerebellar dysfunction (including ataxia, dysarthria, nystagmus and tremor)
evidence.explanation: Lists nystagmus among the cerebellar features.

steps/10.description: Part of the cerebellar syndrome.

evidence.snippet: cerebellar dysfunction (including ataxia, dysarthria, nystagmus and tremor)
evidence.explanation: Lists tremor among the cerebellar features.

steps/11.description: Part of the cerebellar syndrome.

evidence.snippet: global developmental delay, cerebellar dysfunction (including ataxia, dysarthria, nystagmus and tremor) and spasticity
evidence.explanation: Reports spasticity alongside the cerebellar features.

steps/12.description: Pyramidal involvement, reported both in the leukoencephalopathy series and as "pyramidal signs" in the dystonia-predominant kindred.

evidence.snippet: Brain MRI showed cerebellar atrophy.
evidence.explanation: Direct imaging finding in the reported cohort.

steps/13.description: Cerebellar atrophy on brain MRI, present in both reported presentations.

evidence.snippet: To identify the mutated gene in a group of patients with an unclassified heritable white matter disorder sharing the same, distinct MRI pattern.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that these patients were ascertained as a white matter disorder, which is what this phenotype records.

steps/14.description: Deep cerebral white matter and corpus callosum abnormality, part of the pattern that identified this disease.

evidence.snippet: a syndrome characterized by generalized dystonia, pyramidal and cerebellar involvement, with bilateral striatal necrosis (BSN) and cerebellar atrophy on magnetic resonance imaging
evidence.explanation: Reports bilateral striatal necrosis as an imaging finding in this kindred.

steps/15.description: Bilateral striatal necrosis on MRI, reported in the dystonia-predominant UK kindred. HPO has no term for bilateral striatal necrosis specifically, so the binding is to the parent basal ganglia term and the specific finding is carried in preferred_term.

evidence.snippet: Cognition level varies, but is impaired for all except for Patient 2 who has a normal
evidence.explanation: Four of five patients cognitively impaired. Curated because the contrast with the UK kindred's preserved cognition is load-bearing for the open question on this entry - without it the entry would assert only one half of that contrast. Graded FREQUENT rather than VERY_FREQUENT deliberately: 4/5 is nominally 80%, which is the VERY_FREQUENT floor, but at n=5 a single reclassified patient moves the point estimate to 60%, so the band is set from the width of the interval rather than from the point estimate.

steps/16.description: Cognition is impaired in most patients in the leukoencephalopathy series, with one of five having a normal IQ. This is the counterpart of the preserved cognition reported in the UK dystonia kindred, and the two together are what make the relationship between the two presentations an open question rather than a settled spectrum.

evidence.snippet: dysarthria, dysmetria, nystagmus, and intentional tremor), hyperreflexia with clonus,
evidence.explanation: Names hyperreflexia with clonus among the presenting features. The clonus component is recorded separately below, since HPO codes the two distinctly.

steps/17.description: Pyramidal sign reported alongside the cerebellar syndrome at symptom onset. Named for the binding rather than for the source phrase "hyperreflexia with clonus", since the clonus half is curated separately below and HPO codes the two distinctly.

evidence.snippet: dysarthria, dysmetria, nystagmus, and intentional tremor), hyperreflexia with clonus,
evidence.explanation: The same sentence, quoted for the clonus that HPO codes separately from hyperreflexia.

steps/18.description: Reported together with hyperreflexia as part of the pyramidal involvement.

evidence.snippet: dysarthria, dysmetria, nystagmus, and intentional tremor), hyperreflexia with clonus,
evidence.explanation: Names dysmetria within the cerebellar syndrome.

steps/19.description: Part of the cerebellar syndrome. Named in the full-text description of the five patients although absent from the abstract's shorter list.

evidence.snippet: The nucleotide binding protein-like (NUBPL) gene was first reported as a cause of mitochondrial complex I deficiency (MIM 613621, 618242) in 2010. ... The previously reported c.815-27T>C branch-site mutation was found in all four families. In prior patients, c.166G>A ... was always found in cis with c.815-27T>C, but only two of four families had both variants.
evidence.explanation: Names the NUBPL complex-I-deficiency relationship and supplies both the four-family branch-site result and the finding that the previously co-occurring c.166G>A (p.G56R) change is separable from the branch-site allele. Four study families should not alone be interpreted as every reported family; the selected passage does not give the European haplotype frequency. The ellipsis after c.166G>A stands in for the bracketed protein designation, which the reference validator strips from the query side (dismech#10192).

evidence.snippet: Moreover, the mutation is present in 1.2% of European haplotypes.
evidence.explanation: The population frequency that makes the branch-site allele implausible as a fully penetrant dominant lesion and motivated the functional work.

genes/0.notes: Encodes the complex I iron-sulfur cluster assembly factor (yeast Ind1). The recurrent branch-site allele c.815-27T>C is found in every reported family and in about 1.2% of European haplotypes; in the earliest patients it occurred in cis with c.166G>A (p.Gly56Arg), but later families carry it without that variant, so the two are separable.

evidence.snippet: improved with the help of occupational therapy
evidence.explanation: Single patient, uncontrolled, and reported alongside a parent-reported drug effect in the same sentence, so the attribution to occupational therapy alone is not clean.

treatments/0.description: Rehabilitation for the fine motor impairment. Reported to have improved the tremor in one patient, which is the only treatment response in this literature attributed to a specific intervention rather than to a regimen.

evidence.snippet: improved with the help of occupational therapy
evidence.explanation: Attributes the tremor improvement in that patient to occupational therapy.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Symptomatic, not disease-modifying: it addresses the motor consequence and does not act on the assembly defect upstream of it.

evidence.snippet: supplements of coenzyme Q10, carnitine, and α-lipoic
evidence.explanation: Names the three agents that make up the cocktail.

evidence.snippet: new treatments are needed, which are currently limited to
evidence.explanation: The authors' own statement that this is the ceiling of available treatment. Curated because an empty treatments section and a section listing a cocktail read the same to a consumer unless the limit is stated.

treatments/1.description: Coenzyme Q10, carnitine and alpha-lipoic acid. The authors describe this as the current limit of available treatment rather than as an effective therapy, and this entry records it that way: no mechanism link is asserted, because nothing in the cited source shows these agents act on the complex I assembly defect.

evidence.snippet: Supplementary data), from treatment with EPI-743.
evidence.explanation: Names the drug at the patient level. Attribution is weak on its own terms: it is parental report in one patient, in the same sentence that credits occupational therapy.

evidence.snippet: although experimental drugs have shown promise
evidence.explanation: Classes the agent as experimental in the authors' own summary of the field.

treatments/2.description: An experimental agent. One patient's tremor improvement is attributed to it by parental report in the same sentence that credits occupational therapy, so this is recorded as experimental and unevaluated rather than as an effective treatment.

evidence.snippet: Five other patients were recently reported to have NUBPL disease but their clinical picture was different from the first eight patients.
evidence.explanation: States the phenotypic discrepancy directly, without resolving it, which is what makes this an open question rather than a settled spectrum.

evidence.snippet: To date, only eight patients have been reported with this mitochondrial disorder.
evidence.explanation: The total reported cohort at the time of review, which is the sample the whole phenotypic question rests on and is small enough to matter.

open_questions/0.rationale: The review of the genetic and clinical spectrum notes explicitly that a group of patients reported as having NUBPL disease had a clinical picture different from the earlier patients, and does not resolve whether that reflects one spectrum or a different entity. The two published pictures differ in more than emphasis: the original series was ascertained by a white matter MRI pattern, while the UK kindred is dystonia-predominant with bilateral striatal necrosis and specifically preserved cognition. This matters for curation because the entry currently draws both tissue-level nodes downstream of the same complex I deficiency node, which presumes one spectrum. If they are separate entities that reading is wrong. Both edges are marked as indirect with unknown intermediates and both tissue nodes are PROVISIONAL for this reason.

evidence.snippet: It has cutaneous manifestations similar to subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus (SCLE).
evidence.explanation: Entry-level evidence for treating ultraviolet light as a relevant exposure in this disease. Graded PARTIAL deliberately: the abstract establishes the resemblance to SCLE, the archetypal photosensitive lupus dermatosis, and the ultraviolet role is inferred from that rather than stated. No abstract-level source asserting it outright was found, and this entry would rather show the inference than dress it up.

evidence.snippet: Neonatal lupus erythematosus is an autoimmune disease acquired during fetal life as a result of transplacental passage of maternal anti-Sjögren's-syndrome-related antigen A (anti-SSA/Ro), anti-Sjögren's-syndrome-related antigen B (anti-SSB/La) or anti-U1 ribonucleoprotein (anti-U1-RNP) antinuclear autoantibodies.
evidence.explanation: Names the three autoantibody specificities and states that transplacental passage is the acquisition mechanism, which is exactly what this node models.

steps/1.description: Maternal IgG autoantibodies against the Ro/SSA (Ro52/TRIM21 and Ro60) and La/SSB ribonucleoproteins, or against U1-RNP, cross the placenta and enter the fetal circulation. Because placental IgG transport rises through the second and third trimesters, fetal antibody concentration climbs across exactly the gestational window in which the conduction system is vulnerable. This node is the disease's sole initiating event; everything downstream is a consequence of antibody presence in fetal tissue.

evidence.snippet: Recent studies demonstrate that Ro/La ribonucleoproteins appear on the surface of apoptotic fetal cardiocytes and are recognized by their cognate antibodies, promoting an inflammatory response.
evidence.explanation: States the surface translocation of Ro/La on apoptotic fetal cardiocytes and their recognition by the cognate antibodies, which is the claim this node makes. Graded IN_VITRO because the sentence summarises cell-based studies of apoptotic cardiocytes.

steps/2.description: Ro and La are normally intracellular ribonucleoproteins and are therefore invisible to circulating antibody. During the physiological apoptosis that accompanies remodelling of the developing atrioventricular conduction system, these antigens translocate to the surface of apoptotic cardiocytes, where the maternal antibodies can reach them. This developmentally timed unmasking is what confines cardiac injury to a narrow gestational window rather than occurring whenever antibody is present.

evidence.snippet: cardiocytes are capable of phagocytosing autologous apoptotic cardiocytes and anti-Ro/La antibodies inhibit this function
evidence.explanation: The direct statement of this node's mechanism: cardiocyte-mediated clearance of apoptotic cardiocytes exists, and anti-Ro/La antibody inhibits it. Graded IN_VITRO because the phagocytosis assay is a cell-based experiment.

evidence.snippet: Recognizing that this perturbation of physiologic efferocytosis might divert uptake to professional Fc gamma R-bearing phagocytes fits well with experiments demonstrating macrophage secretion of pro-inflammatory and fibrosing cytokines when coincubated with apoptotic cardiocytes bound by Ro/La antibodies.
evidence.explanation: Supports the diversion of clearance to professional phagocytes and the resulting secretion of pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic cytokines, the link from this node to the fibrosis node downstream.

steps/3.description: Healthy cardiocytes normally phagocytose their apoptotic neighbours silently, a form of efferocytosis that produces no inflammation. Bound anti-Ro/La antibody blocks that uptake, so clearance is diverted to professional Fc-gamma-receptor-bearing phagocytes. The same apoptotic cell is then removed through an inflammatory route instead of a silent one. This diversion, rather than the antibody binding itself, is the step that converts a normal developmental process into tissue injury.

evidence.snippet: The identification of exaggerated apoptosis, macrophage/myfibroblast crosstalk, TGF beta expression, and extensive fibrosis in the conducting system and in some cases surrounding myocardium in fetuses dying with CHB, provide in vivo support for several parallel lines of in vitro investigation.
evidence.explanation: Reports the macrophage-myofibroblast crosstalk, TGF-beta expression and conduction-system fibrosis this node models, observed in human fetal tissue rather than in a model system. Graded HUMAN_CLINICAL because the finding is from fetuses dying with congenital heart block.

steps/4.description: Macrophages taking up antibody-bound apoptotic cardiocytes secrete pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrosing cytokines, and crosstalk with myofibroblasts drives TGF-beta expression, extensive fibrosis and dystrophic calcification within the atrioventricular node. Conduction tissue is replaced by scar. The claim that this is structural rather than inflammatory carries the entry's main clinical implication: once replacement is complete the lesion cannot be reversed by suppressing inflammation.

evidence.snippet: Established third-degree block appears to be irreversible.
evidence.explanation: The irreversibility claim that distinguishes this node from the transient manifestations, stated directly.

evidence.snippet: The spectrum of conduction abnormalities includes second and third-degree block, but injury can extend to the myocardium and endocardium, in rare cases without AV nodal dysfunction.
evidence.explanation: Supports both the conduction-block spectrum and the extension of injury beyond the node into myocardium and endocardium, which is what links this node to the cardiomyopathy phenotype.

steps/5.description: Fibrous replacement of the atrioventricular node produces third-degree block: atrial and ventricular activity become fully dissociated and ventricular rate falls to a junctional or ventricular escape rhythm. Most survivors require permanent pacing. Injury may extend beyond the node to the myocardium and endocardium, which is the origin of the late dilated cardiomyopathy and endocardial fibroelastosis seen in some survivors whose in-utero ventricular function was normal.

evidence.snippet: Clinical manifestations include skin lesions, congenital heart block, hepatobiliary involvement and cytopenias. Most of the disorders disappear spontaneously after clearance of maternal antibodies. Cardiac symptoms, however, are not self-resolving and often pacemaker implantation is required.
evidence.explanation: Establishes both halves of the split this node encodes: the non-cardiac manifestations resolve on antibody clearance while the cardiac lesion does not.

steps/6.description: In parallel with the cardiac lesion and by a separate, reversible route, maternal antibody produces annular photosensitive skin lesions, cholestatic or transaminitic liver involvement, and peripheral cytopenias. These manifestations share the cardiac trigger but not its outcome: no fibrotic replacement occurs, so all resolve as maternal IgG is catabolised over the first 6-12 months of life. Modelling them as a distinct node rather than as downstream of the cardiac chain is deliberate, since they occur in infants with entirely normal conduction.

evidence.snippet: It has cutaneous manifestations similar to subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus (SCLE).
evidence.explanation: Graded PARTIAL for the same reason as the photosensitivity phenotype: the resemblance to SCLE, the archetypal photosensitive lupus dermatosis, is what the abstract states, and the UV-exacerbation link is an inference from it rather than a claim this source makes directly. Recorded openly rather than over-graded.

edges/5.description: Ultraviolet exposure aggravates the antibody-mediated cutaneous injury. Attached to the transient arm only: there is no evidence that light exposure influences the cardiac lesion, which forms in utero.

evidence.snippet: Evidence from animal models suggests that reactivity to the p200 region of the Ro52 protein, as well as antibody targeting of L-type calcium channels may be important in the development of cardiac neonatal lupus.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the Ro52 p200 region as the epitope implicated in cardiac disease. Graded MODEL_ORGANISM because the review attributes the finding to animal models.

genes/0.notes: TRIM21 encodes the Ro52 autoantigen. It is listed here as the maternal antibody's molecular target, not as a disease gene: neither mother nor infant carries a pathogenic TRIM21 variant, and the entry asserts no germline cause. Reactivity to the p200 region of Ro52 has been implicated in cardiac disease specifically.

evidence.snippet: Recent studies demonstrate that Ro/La ribonucleoproteins appear on the surface of apoptotic fetal cardiocytes and are recognized by their cognate antibodies, promoting an inflammatory response.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the Ro ribonucleoproteins as the surface-exposed antigens recognised by maternal antibody. Note the source says Ro/La as a pair and does not resolve Ro60 from Ro52, so this supports Ro60 being an antigen rather than singling it out.

genes/1.notes: RO60 (formerly TROVE2) encodes the Ro60 autoantigen. It is listed for the same reason as TRIM21 and SSB - it is a maternal antibody target, not a disease gene - and it is the antigen most directly implicated in the cardiac lesion, since anti-Ro60 binding is the step reported to activate the uPA/plasmin route to TGF-beta. Its earlier absence from this section was an internal inconsistency with the entry description, which names Ro60 among the Ro/SSA components.

evidence.snippet: transplacental passage of maternal anti-Sjögren's-syndrome-related antigen A (anti-SSA/Ro), anti-Sjögren's-syndrome-related antigen B (anti-SSB/La) or anti-U1 ribonucleoprotein (anti-U1-RNP) antinuclear autoantibodies
evidence.explanation: Names anti-SSB/La among the three pathogenic antibody specificities.

genes/2.notes: SSB encodes the La/SSB autoantigen, the second major maternal antibody target. As with TRIM21 this is an antigen, not a disease gene.

evidence.snippet: To date, only anecdotal and retrospective evidence guides in utero therapy of CHB. A prospective trial is currently underway to evaluate the efficacy of maternal oral dexamethasone in treating newly identified first, second or third degree block.
evidence.explanation: Graded PARTIAL, and the grading is the point. The quoted sentence establishes that maternal dexamethasone is the therapy being evaluated, and in the same breath that the evidence for it was anecdotal and retrospective. Recording it as SUPPORT would overstate a treatment the source itself describes as unproven.

evidence.snippet: Established third-degree block appears to be irreversible.
evidence.explanation: The boundary on what this therapy can achieve, and the reason it is attached to the clearance node rather than to the block itself.

treatments/0.description: Fluorinated corticosteroids, principally dexamethasone, given to the mother so that active drug reaches the fetus. This is the therapy behind the entry's central asymmetry: it targets the inflammatory clearance step upstream of fibrosis, so it can act on block that is still evolving and cannot act on block that has already been replaced by scar. Modelled here because the entry states that conclusion in two places, and a conclusion about a therapy should name the therapy. Note the evidence is weak by design of the field rather than by omission - the source below describes only anecdotal and retrospective evidence with a trial then underway.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Acts on the inflammatory clearance route, upstream of fibrotic replacement. This placement is what encodes why the therapy can help before the node fibroses and not after.

evidence.snippet: Dexamethasone and sympathomimetics may be of some benefit in treating hydrops fetalis.
evidence.explanation: Graded PARTIAL because the source says "may be of some benefit", which is a hedge the entry should carry rather than flatten.

treatments/1.description: Sympathomimetic agents, used with dexamethasone, for the fetus that develops hydrops from the bradycardia. This treats the haemodynamic consequence of the block, not the immune lesion, which is why it carries no target_mechanisms link to the pathophysiology chain.

evidence.snippet: Cardiac symptoms, however, are not self-resolving and often pacemaker implantation is required.
evidence.explanation: States both the non-resolution of cardiac disease and the pacemaker requirement that follows from it.

treatments/2.description: Pacemaker implantation is the definitive treatment for established complete block and is required by most survivors. It manages the consequence rather than the cause; no therapy restores conduction once the node is fibrosed.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Restores an adequate ventricular rate downstream of the block. It does not act on the fibrotic lesion.

evidence.snippet: Testing for antinuclear antibodies should be considered in every pregnant woman since early treatment with hydroxychloroquine or intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) has proven to be effective in preventing congenital heart block.
evidence.explanation: States the preventive efficacy of early hydroxychloroquine against congenital heart block, and the word "preventing" is what licenses modelling this as prophylaxis rather than treatment.

evidence.snippet: These prospective data support that HCQ significantly reduces the recurrence of CHB below the historical rate by >50%, suggesting that this drug should be prescribed for secondary prevention of fetal cardiac disease in anti-SSA/Ro-exposed pregnancies.
evidence.explanation: The PATCH trial result, which is the direct prospective evidence for this treatment rather than a guideline restating it. It is also what ties this node to the clinical_trials entry for NCT01379573.

treatments/3.description: Hydroxychloroquine given to an antibody-positive mother, ideally from early pregnancy, is the principal preventive strategy in mothers with a previously affected child. It is prophylaxis against the fibrotic lesion forming, not a treatment for established block.

treatments/3/targets/0.description: Acts upstream of fibrosis, on the inflammatory clearance route, which is consistent with its being effective only as prevention.

evidence.snippet: early treatment with hydroxychloroquine or intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) has proven to be effective in preventing congenital heart block
evidence.explanation: Graded PARTIAL rather than SUPPORT. The guideline groups IVIG with hydroxychloroquine, but the trial evidence for the two is not equivalent, so quoting this sentence as unqualified support for IVIG would overstate what is established.

treatments/4.description: IVIG has been used both preventively in at-risk pregnancies and as an adjunct in established disease. The evidence base is weaker than for hydroxychloroquine and dedicated trials have been largely negative for prevention of recurrence at the doses studied.

evidence.snippet: The cutaneous, hematologic, and hepatic abnormalities are transient, clearing by 6 months of age.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the non-cardiac manifestations are self-limited, which is the rationale for managing them supportively rather than with immunosuppression.

treatments/5.description: Because the rash is photo-provoked and self-limited, management of skin-limited neonatal lupus is protective rather than pharmacological.

treatments/5/targets/0.description: Removes the ultraviolet co-factor while maternal antibody clears.

evidence.snippet: The identification of exaggerated apoptosis, macrophage/myfibroblast crosstalk, TGF beta expression, and extensive fibrosis in the conducting system and in some cases surrounding myocardium in fetuses dying with CHB, provide in vivo support for several parallel lines of in vitro investigation.
evidence.explanation: The human tissue evidence that makes this the canonical account rather than one of two equals.

hypotheses/0.description: The mechanism this entry models in full. Maternal antibody bound to surface-exposed Ro/La on apoptotic cardiocytes blocks their silent clearance by neighbouring cardiocytes, diverting uptake to Fc-gamma-receptor-bearing macrophages, whose pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic secretion drives TGF-beta-mediated fibrosis and permanent replacement of conduction tissue. It is treated as canonical because it is the account with direct human tissue support: fibrosis, TGF-beta expression and macrophage-myofibroblast crosstalk have been observed in fetuses dying with congenital heart block.

evidence.snippet: Evidence from animal models suggests that reactivity to the p200 region of the Ro52 protein, as well as antibody targeting of L-type calcium channels may be important in the development of cardiac neonatal lupus.
evidence.explanation: Names antibody targeting of L-type calcium channels as a candidate mechanism. Graded MODEL_ORGANISM because the review attributes it to animal models, which is also why it is ALTERNATIVE rather than CANONICAL - the fibrosis account has human tissue support and this one does not yet.

evidence.snippet: These antibodies may induce a myocarditis, or interact directly with calcium channel proteins with disturbance of transmembrane signaling at the level of the conduction tissue, or interfere with apoptosis.
evidence.explanation: States all three candidate routes side by side, including the direct calcium-channel interaction this hypothesis group names. The source's own "may" is why the group is ALTERNATIVE.

hypotheses/1.description: A complementary account in which anti-Ro/La antibodies cross-react directly with cardiac L-type and T-type calcium channels, disturbing transmembrane calcium signalling in conduction tissue and impairing conduction without requiring inflammation. This is not a rival that would make the fibrosis account wrong: the two operate on different timescales, and a direct channel effect is the more natural explanation for the conduction abnormalities that are reversible, while fibrosis explains the ones that are not. It is recorded as ALTERNATIVE rather than modelled as its own node chain because no node in this entry currently rests on it, and inventing one would assert more than the cited sources do.

evidence.snippet: All patients with types A and B NPD have mutations in the gene encoding ASM (SMPD1), and thus the disease is more accurately referred to as ASM deficiency (ASMD).
evidence.explanation: SMPD1 mutation and acid sphingomyelinase deficiency underlie NPD type B.

steps/1.description: Biallelic SMPD1 variants reduce but do not abolish acid sphingomyelinase activity. The residual activity is generally sufficient to spare the CNS, so disease is dominated by visceral sphingomyelin storage rather than neurodegeneration.

evidence.snippet: Type B patients also have hepatosplenomegaly and pathologic alterations of their lungs, but there are usually no CNS signs.
evidence.explanation: Visceral and pulmonary storage with CNS sparing defines NPD-B.

steps/2.description: Sphingomyelin accumulates in macrophages of the spleen, liver, lung, and bone marrow, forming lipid-laden foam cells. The reticuloendothelial and pulmonary storage burden drives the visceral manifestations of NPD-B with relative sparing of the CNS.

evidence.snippet: Almost all patients have hepatosplenomegaly and an atherogenic lipid profile
evidence.explanation: Hepatosplenomegaly is near-universal in NPD-B.

steps/3.description: Enlargement of liver and spleen from sphingomyelin-laden foam cells.

evidence.snippet: hematologic abnormalities including cytopenias
evidence.explanation: Cytopenias including thrombocytopenia are characteristic.

steps/4.description: Cytopenias, especially thrombocytopenia, from hypersplenism and marrow involvement.

evidence.snippet: most patients have interstitial lung disease with progressive impairment of pulmonary function
evidence.explanation: Interstitial lung disease is a major feature of NPD-B.

steps/5.description: Progressive interstitial lung disease with impaired diffusion capacity.

evidence.snippet: Almost all patients have hepatosplenomegaly and an atherogenic lipid profile

evidence.snippet: CREB3L1 encodes OASIS, an endoplasmic reticulum-stress transducer that regulates type I procollagen expression during murine bone formation.

evidence.snippet: OASIS is processed by regulated intramembrane proteolysis (RIP) in response to ER stress, and is highly expressed in osteoblasts.

evidence.snippet: the endoplasmic reticulum stress transducer old astrocyte specifically induced substance (OASIS), which has an important role in osteoblast differentiation during bone development.

steps/1.description: CREB3L1 encodes OASIS, a bZIP transcription factor of the CREB/ATF family that has a transmembrane domain and is processed by regulated intramembrane proteolysis (RIP) in response to ER stress; it is highly expressed in osteoblasts. Biallelic loss-of-function CREB3L1 variants (the original 11p11.2 contiguous deletion, premature stop codons, or missense variants in the bZIP domain) eliminate or inactivate OASIS. OASIS expression and its RIP processing are induced by BMP2 signaling, which is required for bone formation, linking ER-stress-induced OASIS signaling to osteoblast function.

evidence.snippet: Here we identify the gene for type 1 collagen, Col1a1, as a target of OASIS, and demonstrate that OASIS activates the transcription of Col1a1 through an unfolded protein response element (UPRE)-like sequence in the osteoblast-specific Col1a1 promoter region.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that OASIS transcriptionally activates COL1A1, the function whose loss reduces type I collagen synthesis in OI type XVI.

evidence.snippet: In vitro structural modeling and luciferase assays demonstrate that this missense variant affects a critical residue in this functional domain, thereby decreasing the type I collagen transcriptional binding ability.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that a pathogenic CREB3L1 bZIP-domain missense variant decreases OASIS-mediated type I collagen transcriptional activation.

evidence.snippet: Markedly low levels of CREB3L1 mRNA were confirmed by qPCR in hOBs (16%) and FB (21%); however, collagen I levels were only reduced in hOBs (5-10%).
evidence.explanation: Documents markedly reduced CREB3L1 expression and an osteoblast-specific reduction of type I collagen in OASIS-deficient human cells.

steps/2.description: OASIS directly activates transcription of the type I collagen gene COL1A1 through an unfolded protein response element (UPRE)-like sequence in the osteoblast-specific Col1a1 promoter and contributes to the secretion of bone matrix proteins. When OASIS is lost or its DNA-binding/bZIP activity is impaired, COL1A1 transcriptional activation falls and osteoblasts synthesize markedly less type I collagen. In OASIS-deficient human osteoblasts, CREB3L1 mRNA and collagen I are reduced and the rough ER is ultrastructurally abnormal; in mice, OASIS-/- osteoblasts show decreased type I collagen in the bone matrix and an abnormally expanded rough ER engorged with bone matrix proteins, reflecting impaired collagen production and secretion.

evidence.snippet: OASIS(-/-) mice exhibited severe osteopenia, involving a decrease in type I collagen in the bone matrix and a decline in the activity of osteoblasts, which showed abnormally expanded rough ER, containing of a large amount of bone matrix proteins.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that OASIS loss produces a collagen-poor bone matrix and severe osteopenia, the matrix defect underlying OI type XVI fragility.

evidence.snippet: Bone histomorphometry and qBEI were similar to collagen I OI, with low trabecular thickness and mineral apposition rate, and increased bone matrix mineralization.
evidence.explanation: Documents the abnormal human bone matrix (low trabecular thickness and mineral apposition) underlying the skeletal fragility of OI type XVI.

steps/3.description: Reduced osteoblast type I collagen production yields a defective, collagen-deficient bone extracellular matrix with low trabecular thickness, reduced mineral apposition, and impaired mechanical strength, producing very low bone mass and severe skeletal fragility. Clinically this manifests as recurrent prenatal and postnatal fractures, reduced bone mineral density, growth deficiency, and bone deformity. The OASIS-deficient (OASIS-/-) mouse recapitulates the disorder with severe osteopenia, decreased bone-matrix type I collagen, dysfunctional osteoblasts, and spontaneous fractures.

edges/1.description: Loss of OASIS removes the transcriptional activator that drives osteoblast-specific COL1A1 expression, reducing type I collagen synthesis and bone-matrix protein secretion.

edges/2.description: Deficient osteoblast type I collagen synthesis produces a collagen-poor, defective bone extracellular matrix with low bone mass and reduced mechanical strength.

genes/0.notes: OI type XVI is caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in CREB3L1, encoding the ER-stress transducer OASIS. The disorder was first defined by a homozygous 11p11.2 contiguous genomic deletion encompassing CREB3L1 in a family with severe OI. Subsequent reports established point-variant alleles, including a homozygous premature stop (nonsense) codon in the first patient to survive infancy and a homozygous pathogenic missense variant [p.(Ala304Val)] in the highly conserved basic leucine zipper domain, four amino acids upstream of the DNA-binding domain, in a patient with lethal OI. Heterozygous carriers show a mild or no phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Histological and histomorphometric analyses revealed that the trabecular bones increased dramatically in OASIS-/- mice treated with RIS, owing to the inhibition of bone resorption.

treatments/0.description: Intravenous bisphosphonates (e.g., pamidronate, zoledronic acid) are the pharmacological mainstay of severe OI, increasing bone mineral density and reducing fracture frequency; in OI type XVI, life-long bisphosphonate treatment steadily increased bone mineral density although fractures persisted. They are antiresorptive and do not correct the underlying transcriptional collagen defect. The OASIS-deficient mouse responds to risedronate with increased trabecular bone, supporting bisphosphonate efficacy in this disorder.

treatments/1.description: Intramedullary (telescoping) rod fixation and corrective osteotomy stabilize fracture-prone, deformed long bones; spinal surgery addresses progressive scoliosis. Surgical management is standard in severe OI such as OI type XVI.
